articles.title: Best student loans for nursing school

paras.en: Federal student loans are an important source of funding for nursing school, but they may not cover the full cost. That's especially relevant for graduate and professional nursing students following federal loan changes that took effect July 1, 2026. New borrowing limits are now in place, and most new graduate and professional students can no longer use Grad PLUS Loans to borrow up to the full cost of attendance.
paras.zh: 联邦学生贷款是护士学校的重要资金来源，但它们可能无法支付全部费用。这对于 2026 年 7 月 1 日生效的联邦贷款变更后的研究生和专业护理学生尤其重要。新的借款限额现已到位，大多数新的研究生和专业学生不能再使用研究生加贷款来借款至全额出勤费用。

paras.en: For eligible professional students, federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans are generally capped at $50,000 per year and $200,000 in aggregate, although certain health-professions programs have additional rules and exceptions. If your nursing program costs more than your available federal aid, you may need another way to cover the remaining balance.
paras.zh: 对于符合条件的专业学生，联邦直接无补贴贷款的上限通常为每年 50,000 美元，总计 200,000 美元，尽管某些健康专业项目有额外的规则和例外。如果您的护理计划的费用超过您可用的联邦援助，您可能需要其他方式来支付剩余余额。

paras.en: That's where private student loans come in. Private lenders can provide additional funding when federal loans and other resources don't cover your total education costs. However, private loans generally don't offer the same federal protections and benefits, so it's important to compare rates, fees, repayment terms and borrower protections before taking one out.
paras.zh: 这就是私人学生贷款的用武之地。当联邦贷款和其他资源无法支付您的总教育费用时，私人贷款机构可以提供额外资金。然而，私人贷款通常不提供相同的联邦保护和福利，因此在贷款之前比较利率、费用、还款条件和借款人保护非常重要。

paras.en: Below, we rounded up some of the best private student loans for nursing school. Note that eligibility may depend on your specific nursing program and school. You can read our methodology below.
paras.zh: 下面，我们收集了一些适合护士学校的最佳私人学生贷款。请注意，资格可能取决于您的具体护理项目和学校。您可以阅读下面我们的方法。

paras.en: Offers in this section are from affiliate partners and selected based on a combination of engagement, product relevance, compensation, and consistent availability.
paras.zh: 此部分中的优惠来自联属合作伙伴，并根据参与度、产品相关性、报酬和一致可用性的组合进行选择。

paras.en: Undergraduate and graduate students, parents, students in MBA, law, health professional and dental programs
paras.zh: 本科生和研究生、家长、MBA、法律、健康专业和牙科项目的学生

paras.en: $5,000 (or state-mandated minimum) up to the cost of attendance
paras.zh: 5,000 美元（或州规定的最低限额），最高可达出席费用

paras.en: 5, 7, 10, 15, years; up to 20 years for refinancing loans
paras.zh: 5、7、10、15 年；再融资贷款期限最长可达 20 年

paras.en: Undergraduate, graduate, Master's, PhD, MBA, law school, medical school, health professions, dental school, medical and dental residency loans, bar study loans.
paras.zh: 本科生、研究生、硕士、博士、MBA、法学院、医学院、健康专业、牙科学校、医疗和牙科住院医师贷款、律师学习贷款。

paras.en: $1,000 up to 100% of the cost of attendance
paras.zh: 1,000 美元，最高可达 100% 的出勤费用

paras.en: - $25/month partial interest payment option available while you are enrolled at least half-time
paras.zh: - 当您注册至少一半时间时，可以选择每月 25 美元的部分利息支付选项

paras.en: - 0.25% interest rate discount for autopay
paras.zh: - 自动转帐可享 0.25% 利率折扣

paras.en: - Co-signers eligible for release after 12 consecutive payments
paras.zh: - 连续 12 次付款后，联合签名者有资格获得释放

paras.en: - Offers a $250 bonus to eligible borrowers with a 3.0 GPA or better
paras.zh: - 向 GPA 达到 3.0 或更高的合格借款人提供 250 美元的奖金

paras.en: - Existing SoFi members may qualify for an additional rate discount
paras.zh: - 现有 SoFi 会员可能有资格享受额外的利率折扣

paras.en: - Good to excellent credit is typically required for approval
paras.zh: - 批准通常需要良好到优秀的信用

paras.en: - $5,000 minimum loan amount is higher than other lenders' minimums.
paras.zh: - 5,000 美元的最低贷款金额高于其他贷方的最低贷款金额。

paras.en: Interest Rates: Eligibility and Important Details. Fixed rates range from 2.99% APR to 15.99% APR with 0.25% autopay discount. Variable rates range from 4.64% APR to 15.99% APR with a 0.25% autopay discount. Unless required to be lower to comply with applicable law, Variable Interest rates are capped at 17.95%. SoFi rate ranges are current as of 9/3/2026 and are subject to change at any time. Your actual rate will be within the range of rates listed above and will depend on the term and type of repayment option you select, evaluation of your creditworthiness, income, presence of a co-signer (if applicable) and a variety of other factors. Lowest rates reserved for the most creditworthy borrowers. Check out our eligibility criteria at https://www.sofi.com/eligibility-criteria/. For the SoFi variable-rate product, the variable interest rate for a given month is derived by adding a margin to the 30-day average SOFR index, published two business days preceding such calendar month, rounded up to the nearest one hundredth of one percent (0.01% or 0.0001). APRs for variable-rate loans may increase after origination if the SOFR index increases.
paras.zh: 利率：资格和重要细节。固定利率范围为年利率 2.99% 至 15.99%，并有 0.25% 自动转账折扣。可变利率范围为年利率 4.64% 至 15.99%，并有 0.25% 自动转账折扣。除非为了遵守适用法律而要求降低，否则可变利率的上限为 17.95%。 SoFi 费率范围截至 2026 年 9 月 3 日有效，并可能随时更改。您的实际利率将在上面列出的利率范围内，并将取决于您选择的还款选项的期限和类型、对您的信用度的评估、收入、共同签名人的存在（如果适用）以及各种其他因素。为最信誉良好的借款人保留最低利率。请访问 https://www.sofi.com/eligibility-criteria/ 查看我们的资格标准。对于 SoFi 可变利率产品，给定月份的可变利率是通过在该日历月前两个工作日发布的 30 天平均 SOFR 指数中添加保证金得出的，四舍五入到最接近的百分之一（0.01% 或 0.0001）。如果 SOFR 指数增加，可变利率贷款的年利率可能会在发放后增加。

paras.en: Who's this for? SoFi is a good fit for borrowers who value extra member benefits alongside their student loan. Members can get access to career coaching, personalized financial planning and a discount on additional SoFi loans.
paras.zh: 这是给谁的？ SoFi 非常适合那些除了学生贷款之外还重视额外会员福利的借款人。会员可以获得职业指导、个性化财务规划以及额外 SoFi 贷款折扣。

paras.en: Standout benefits: SoFi offers deferment and forbearance options for eligible borrowers, which aren't available from every private lender. It also offers hardship options that may allow eligible borrowers experiencing unemployment or other financial difficulties to temporarily reduce or postpone payments.
paras.zh: 突出的好处：SoFi 为符合条件的借款人提供延期和延期选项，而并非所有私人贷款机构都提供这些选项。它还提供困难选项，可以允许遇到失业或其他财务困难的合格借款人暂时减少或推迟还款。

paras.en: - Eligible borrowers Qualifying juniors, seniors and graduate students
paras.zh: - 符合资格的借款人 合格的大三学生、大四学生和研究生

paras.en: - Loan amounts $2,000 up to $15,000 per academic year and up to $10,000 for summer terms; ($20,000 lifetime limit)
paras.zh: - 每学年贷款金额为 2,000 美元至 15,000 美元，夏季学期贷款金额高达 10,000 美元； （终身限额 20,000 美元）

paras.en: - Borrower protections Deferment and forbearance; all loans are based on income-based repayment
paras.zh: - 借款人保护 延期和延期；所有贷款均基于收入还款

paras.en: - Considers borrowers' schooling and programs
paras.zh: - 考虑借款人的教育和项目

paras.en: - Student success team and career counselors available for support
paras.zh: - 学生成功团队和职业顾问可提供支持

paras.en: - Non-cosigned loans tend to charge higher interest rates
paras.zh: - 非联署贷款往往收取更高的利率

paras.en: Who's this for? Edly may be a good fit for borrowers who want the option to release a co-signer relatively quickly. Eligible borrowers can request co-signer release after making six consecutive, in-full monthly payments after graduation, subject to credit and other requirements. That's the shortest payment requirement among the lenders on this list.
paras.zh: 这是给谁的？ Edly 可能非常适合那些希望能够相对较快地释放联合签名人的借款人。符合资格的借款人可以在毕业后连续六次每月全额还款后请求联合签署人释放，但须遵守信用和其他要求。这是该名单上的贷方中最短的付款要求。

paras.en: Standout benefits: Edly's student loans use income-based repayment, meaning your monthly payment adjusts based on your income. Edly also offers deferment and forbearance options for eligible borrowers facing financial hardship.
paras.zh: 突出的好处：Edly 的学生贷款采用基于收入的还款方式，这意味着您的每月还款额根据您的收入进行调整。 Edly 还为面临财务困难的合格借款人提供延期和延期选择。

paras.en: - Co-signer release available after just 12 payments
paras.zh: - 只需 12 次付款即可获得联合签名者释放

paras.en: - Up to 1% interest rate discount for autopay*
paras.zh: - 自动转帐高达 1% 利率折扣*

paras.en: - Considers alternative requirements like the borrower’s school, program, graduation date, major, GPA, cost of attendance and Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) to grant approval
paras.zh: - 考虑借款人的学校、课程、毕业日期、专业、GPA、就读费用和令人满意的学业进步 (SAP) 等替代要求以授予批准

paras.en: - Doesn't offer student loan refinancing
paras.zh: - 不提供学生贷款再融资

paras.en: Who's this for? Ascent may be a good fit for borrowers who want more time before repayment begins. Its graduate and health-profession loans offer a 9-month grace period, compared with the six months that's more common among private lenders.
paras.zh: 这是给谁的？对于希望在还款开始前有更多时间的借款人来说，Ascent 可能是一个不错的选择。它的研究生和医疗专业贷款提供 9 个月的宽限期，而私人贷款机构更常见的是 6 个月的宽限期。

paras.en: Standout benefits: Ascent offers benefits including a 0.50% to 1.00% automatic payment discount, college and career coaching, the option to apply for co-signer release after 12 consecutive on-time payments and more.
paras.zh: 突出的好处：Ascent 提供的好处包括 0.50% 至 1.00% 的自动付款折扣、大学和职业指导、连续 12 次按时付款后申请共同签署人释放的选项等等。

paras.en: - Loans available to part-time and continuing ed students
paras.zh: - 向非全日制和继续教育学生提供贷款

paras.en: - Co-signer release after just 12 payments
paras.zh: - 联合签名者只需 12 次付款后即可释放

paras.en: - Offers loans for a wide variety of educational needs including: bar study, medical school, residency and relocation costs, dental school, residency and relocation costs, nursing school/health professions, commercial flight school, coding boot camp and professional certifications
paras.zh: - 为各种教育需求提供贷款，包括：律师学习、医学院、住院和搬迁费用、牙科学校、住院和搬迁费用、护士学校/健康专业、商业飞行学校、编码训练营和专业认证

paras.en: Who's this for? Sallie Mae doesn't charge origination fees on its student loans, which is a fee some lenders charge to process a loan and it can reduce the amount you receive.
paras.zh: 这是给谁的？ Sallie Mae 不收取学生贷款发起费，这是一些贷方在处理贷款时收取的费用，它可以减少您收到的金额。

paras.en: Standout benefits: Eligible borrowers can defer payments for up to 48 months during residency or fellowship, depending on the loan. Keep in mind that interest continues to accrue during deferment, which can increase the total cost of the loan.
paras.zh: 突出的好处：符合条件的借款人可以在住院医师或研究员期间推迟付款最多 48 个月，具体取决于贷款。请记住，延期期间利息会继续累积，这可能会增加贷款的总成本。

paras.en: How long does it take to remove a co-signer from a student loan?
paras.zh: 从学生贷款中删除共同签署人需要多长时间？

paras.en: The number of monthly payments a borrower must make before they can release their co-signer varies by lender. The fewest we've found is six months, but with some lenders, you may have to wait at least 1 to 2 years to be eligible for a co-signer release.
paras.zh: 借款人在释放其共同签署人之前必须每月还款的次数因贷方而异。我们发现的最少期限是六个月，但对于某些贷方，您可能需要等待至少 1 到 2 年才有资格获得共同签署人释放。

paras.en: Fees can vary by lender. Some lenders don't charge origination fees or application fees, but you should always double check the terms of your loan before accepting an offer.
paras.zh: 费用可能因贷方而异。有些贷方不收取启动费或申请费，但在接受报价之前，您应该仔细检查贷款条款。

paras.en: Can you defer payments for nursing school loans?
paras.zh: 您可以推迟支付护士学校贷款吗？

paras.en: Some lenders offer a grace period of 6 or 9 months after graduation to help you transition back into making loan payments. Other lenders may offer special deferment periods while you're in a residency program.
paras.zh: 一些贷方在毕业后提供 6 或 9 个月的宽限期，以帮助您重新开始支付贷款。当您参加居住计划时，其他贷方可能会提供特殊的延期期限。

paras.en: At CNBC Select, our mission is to provide our readers with high-quality service journalism and comprehensive consumer advice so they can make informed decisions with their money. Every student loan list is based on rigorous reporting by our team of expert writers and editors with extensive knowledge of student loan products. While CNBC Select earns a commission from affiliate partners on many offers and links, we create all our content without input from our commercial team or any outside third parties, and we pride ourselves on our journalistic standards and ethics.
paras.zh: 在 CNBC Select，我们的使命是为读者提供高质量的服务新闻和全面的消费者建议，以便他们能够用自己的钱做出明智的决定。每份学生贷款清单均基于我们对学生贷款产品拥有丰富知识的专家作家和编辑团队的严格报告。虽然 CNBC Select 通过许多优惠和链接从附属合作伙伴那里赚取佣金，但我们在创建所有内容时都没有来自我们的商业团队或任何外部第三方的投入，我们对我们的新闻标准和道德感到自豪。

paras.en: To determine which private student loan providers offer the best loans for nursing school, CNBC Select compared dozens of lenders and categorized them by best for borrower benefits, best for co-signer release, best for grace period and best for no origination fee.
paras.zh: 为了确定哪些私人学生贷款提供商为护理学校提供最好的贷款，CNBC Select 比较了数十家贷款机构，并将它们按照最有利于借款人利益、最有利于共同签署人释放、最有宽限期和最无启动费进行分类。

paras.en: We also rated them on criteria, including:
paras.zh: 我们还根据标准对它们进行了评级，包括：

paras.en: - Application requirements, including credit score and income requirements
paras.zh: - 申请要求，包括信用评分和收入要求

paras.en: - The number of payments before a co-signer can be released
paras.zh: - 联合签名者可以被释放之前的付款次数

paras.en: - Whether it charges application and origination fees or a prepayment penalty
paras.zh: - 是否收取申请费和发起费或预付款罚金

paras.en: - The variety of loan repayment terms available
paras.zh: - 提供多种贷款还款条件

paras.en: - Whether borrowers can access hardship relief, including deferment and forbearance
paras.zh: - 借款人是否可以获得困难救济，包括延期和宽恕

paras.en: Interest Rates: Eligibility and Important Details. Fixed rates range from 2.99% APR to 15.99% APR with 0.25% autopay discount. Variable rates range from 4.64% APR to 15.99% APR with a 0.25% autopay discount. Unless required to be lower to comply with applicable law, Variable Interest rates are capped at 17.95%. SoFi rate ranges are current as of 9/3/2026 and are subject to change at any time. Your actual rate will be within the range of rates listed above and will depend on the term and type of repayment option you select, evaluation of your creditworthiness, income, presence of a co-signer (if applicable) and a variety of other factors. Lowest rates reserved for the most creditworthy borrowers. Check out our eligibility criteria at https://www.sofi.com/eligibility-criteria/. For the SoFi variable-rate product, the variable interest rate for a given month is derived by adding a margin to the 30-day average SOFR index, published two business days preceding such calendar month, rounded up to the nearest one hundredth of one percent (0.01% or 0.0001). APRs for variable-rate loans may increase after origination if the SOFR index increases.
paras.zh: 利率：资格和重要细节。固定利率范围为年利率 2.99% 至 15.99%，并有 0.25% 自动转账折扣。可变利率范围为年利率 4.64% 至 15.99%，并有 0.25% 自动转账折扣。除非为了遵守适用法律而要求降低，否则可变利率的上限为 17.95%。 SoFi 费率范围截至 2026 年 9 月 3 日有效，并可能随时更改。您的实际利率将在上面列出的利率范围内，并将取决于您选择的还款选项的期限和类型、对您的信用度的评估、收入、共同签名人的存在（如果适用）以及各种其他因素。为最信誉良好的借款人保留最低利率。请访问 https://www.sofi.com/eligibility-criteria/ 查看我们的资格标准。对于 SoFi 可变利率产品，给定月份的可变利率是通过在该日历月前两个工作日发布的 30 天平均 SOFR 指数中添加保证金得出的，四舍五入到最接近的百分之一（0.01% 或 0.0001）。如果 SOFR 指数增加，可变利率贷款的年利率可能会在发放后增加。

paras.en: Autopay Discount: The SoFi 0.25% autopay interest rate reduction requires you to agree to make monthly payments as outlined in your loan agreement by an automatic monthly deduction from a savings or checking account. This benefit will discontinue and be lost for periods in which you do not pay by automatic deduction from a savings or checking account. When the autopay interest rate deduction is added or removed, the next time the loan is re-amortized (quarterly for fixed rate loans; monthly for variable rate loans),the principal balance of your loan will be spread over the remaining loan term, and your monthly payment amount will change. This benefit is suspended during periods of deferment, grace period, or forbearance. Autopay is not required to receive a loan from SoFi.
paras.zh: 自动付款折扣：SoFi 0.25% 自动付款利率降低要求您同意按照贷款协议中的规定每月从储蓄或支票账户中自动扣除费用。如果您未从储蓄或支票账户自动扣除费用，则此福利将终止并丢失。当添加或取消自动转账利率扣除后，下次贷款重新摊销时（固定利率贷款按季度；浮动利率贷款按月），您的贷款本金余额将分摊到剩余贷款期限内，您的每月还款金额也会发生变化。此福利在延期、宽限期或宽容期间暂停。从 SoFi 获得贷款不需要自动转账。

articles.title: How event contract bundles are boosting volume on prediction markets

paras.en: The growing popularity of a combo contracts on prediction markets is leading to soaring volumes, even as they makes up only a small amount of total activity on the platforms.
paras.zh: 组合合约在预测市场上越来越受欢迎，导致交易量飙升，尽管它们只占平台总活动的一小部分。

paras.en: Combos, or multiple contracts stacked together that only pay out if all of them win — similar to parlays on traditional sportsbooks — have exploded in popularity.
paras.zh: 组合投注，即多个合同叠加在一起，只有在全部获胜的情况下才能支付的奖金——类似于传统体育博彩的连赢投注——已经大受欢迎。

paras.en: Last month, combos accounted for more than 50% of notional volume on Kalshi, driven by the start of the NFL season. Combos are overwhelmingly made up of combinations of multiple sports contracts.
paras.zh: 上个月，受 NFL 赛季开始的推动，组合占 Kalshi 名义交易量的 50% 以上。组合绝大多数由多个体育合同的组合组成。

paras.en: As rival Polymarket worked to expand its U.S. exchange this year, combos were a priority following the domestic platform's official launch in May. Combos are now nearly 50% of daily volume on Polymarket U.S., helped by growth during the NFL season.
paras.zh: 随着竞争对手 Polymarket 今年致力于扩大其美国交易所，自 5 月份国内平台正式推出以来，组合成为了首要任务。得益于 NFL 赛季的增长，组合商品目前占 Polymarket U.S. 每日交易量的近 50%。

paras.en: But while combos hold a large share of volume, they actually aren't where most speculators on prediction markets execute their trades. That's because of how the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal regulator overseeing prediction markets, requires exchanges to report volume.
paras.zh: 但是，虽然组合占据了很大的交易量份额，但它们实际上并不是预测市场上大多数投机者执行交易的地方。这是因为监管预测市场的联邦监管机构商品期货交易委员会要求交易所报告交易量。

paras.en: The multi-leg contracts are "helping [Polymarket and Kalshi] claim a higher number with lower realistic cash output," said Chris Park, a researcher and founder of MSR Decode, a research firm analyzing prediction market data.
paras.zh: 分析预测市场数据的研究公司MSR Decode的研究员兼创始人克里斯·帕克(Chris Park)表示，多边合同“帮助Polymarket和Kalshi以较低的实际现金产出获得更高的数字”。

paras.en: When a trader places a trade on a prediction market, no matter the cash they put down, platforms measure it as $1 of notional volume. All event contracts have binary outcomes between $0 to $1, and no matter what price a speculator pays to place a trade, someone has to take the other side of that order and make $1 in total volume.
paras.zh: 当交易者在预测市场上进行交易时，无论他们投入多少现金，平台都会将其计算为 1 美元的名义交易量。所有事件合约的二元结果都在 0 美元到 1 美元之间，无论投机者支付多少价格进行交易，都必须有人采取该订单的另一方并赚取 1 美元的总交易量。

paras.en: But combos can have payouts that are much greater than $1, meaning someone can put very little money down, pennies in some cases, and it will be measured as potentially thousands of dollars in volume thanks to the market makers who take the other side of these high-payout trades.
paras.zh: 但组合的支出可能远高于 1 美元，这意味着有人可以投入很少的钱，在某些情况下是几美分，而由于做市商在这些高支出交易的另一边，它的交易量将被衡量为潜在的数千美元。

paras.en: A CNBC analysis for trades on Kalshi on Sept. 27 showed this in practice. On single contracts, the average amount of cash placed on a trade was less than 47 cents. But on combo contracts, that average per contract was about 9 cents.
paras.zh: CNBC 9 月 27 日对 Kalshi 交易的分析在实践中证明了这一点。对于单一合约，一笔交易的平均现金金额不到 47 美分。但对于组合合约，每份合约的平均价格约为 9 美分。

paras.en: Similarly, while combos comprised 58% of Kalshi's trading volume in September, they made up less than 13% of the total transactions on the platform, according to data on Dune.
paras.zh: 同样，根据 Dune 的数据，虽然组合占 Kalshi 9 月份交易量的 58%，但占平台总交易量的比例不到 13%。

paras.en: Other than sports, combos trump other categories for notional volume on Kalshi, with over 35% total volume share.
paras.zh: 除了运动之外，组合在 Kalshi 上的名义交易量超过了其他类别，占总交易量份额的 35% 以上。

paras.en: Details on how combos are measured is not always clear to the public, but their effect on total headline volume numbers can make platforms look as though they're growing faster than they are.
paras.zh: 公众并不总是清楚如何衡量组合的详细信息，但它们对头条新闻总销量的影响可能会让平台看起来增长速度比实际要快。

paras.en: The rising popularity of prediction markets' sports-related event contracts has hurt traditional online sportsbooks — including FanDuel parent Flutter Entertainment, and DraftKings — whose stocks have plunged 70% and 45%, respectively, over the past year.
paras.zh: 预测市场体育相关赛事合约的日益普及，损害了传统在线体育博彩公司——包括 FanDuel 母公司 Flutter Entertainment 和 DraftKings——它们的股价在过去一年里分别暴跌了 70% 和 45%。

paras.en: But some note that investors may be confusing activity numbers that aren't exactly comparable.
paras.zh: 但一些人指出，投资者可能会对不完全可比的活动数据感到困惑。

paras.en: "I have spoken to investors who see the notional number and compare it to [the] handle in sports betting, and then make the argument that. you know, these prediction markets have already exceeded [the] scale of sports betting," said Ian Moore, an analyst at Bernstein.
paras.zh: 伯恩斯坦分析师伊恩·摩尔表示：“我曾与投资者交谈过，他们看到了名义数字，并将其与体育博彩的手柄进行比较，然后提出论点。你知道，这些预测市场已经超过了体育博彩的规模。”

paras.en: A "handle" in a sportsbook measures the total dollar amount wagered, while prediction markets count both sides of a trade.
paras.zh: 体育博彩中的“手柄”衡量的是下注的总金额，而预测市场则计算交易的双方。

paras.en: "When a client buys a deep out-of-the-money contract or a combo, prediction markets may have dollar volumes anywhere between 20 to 100 times greater than sportsbooks because CFTC reporting requires one thing and sportsbooks report the same activity differently," said Rich Jaycobs, an independent advisor to prediction markets seeking regulatory approval from the CFTC. "Same basic bet, same basic idea, but you're getting a completely different perception of activity."
paras.zh: “当客户购买深度虚值合约或组合合约时，预测市场的交易量可能是体育博彩公司的 20 到 100 倍，因为 CFTC 报告要求一件事，而体育博彩公司以不同的方式报告相同的活动，”寻求 CFTC 监管批准的预测市场独立顾问 Rich Jaycobs 表示。 “相同的基本赌注，相同的基本想法，但你对活动的看法完全不同。”

paras.en: Kalshi said its notional volume doesn't overstate activity. "If people are more interested in other measurements, they can look at other metrics," said spokesperson Jack Such.
paras.zh: 卡尔希表示，其名义交易量并没有夸大活动。 “如果人们对其他衡量标准更感兴趣，他们可以查看其他指标，”发言人杰克·萨奇（Jack Such）说。

paras.en: While notional volume is the standard metric for prediction markets, some have suggested looking instead at taker volume as a better measurement. That's because "takers" scoop up liquidity from market makers, rather than provide it, and thus can be a better yardstick of where activity is on exchanges.
paras.zh: 虽然名义交易量是预测市场的标准指标，但一些人建议将接受者交易量视为更好的衡量标准。这是因为“接受者”从做市商那里获取流动性，而不是提供流动性，因此可以更好地衡量交易所的活动情况。

paras.en: "We really like to look at taker volume in terms of buying yes on combos," said Kyle Gesuelli, the company's head of revenue and analytics. That measures trader demand for bets where the all the combined outcomes turn true. "That feels like a better measure for us to just truly understand the underlying activity."
paras.zh: 该公司收入和分析主管凯尔·格苏利 (Kyle Gesuelli) 表示：“我们真的很喜欢通过购买组合来查看接受者的数量。”这衡量了交易者对所有综合结果都为真的投注的需求。 “这感觉是我们真正了解潜在活动的更好衡量标准。”

paras.en: Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.
paras.zh: 披露：CNBC 和 Kalshi 之间存在商业关系，包括客户获取和少数股权投资。

articles.title: Meta joins with group of companies to tame ‘chaos’ of doing business with AI bots

paras.en: A month after Meta's launch of Muse, the personal agent that quickly turned into a viral sensation, a group of companies is coming together to try to simplify the process of bringing the technology into the business world.
paras.zh: Meta 推出个人代理 Muse 一个月后迅速引起轰动，一些公司齐心协力，试图简化将该技术引入商业世界的过程。

paras.en: Meta, Walmart, Stripe and a handful of other companies are publishing what they're calling a "personal agent protocol." It's an open standard meant to dictate how artificial intelligence agents can interact with businesses.
paras.zh: Meta、沃尔玛、Stripe 和其他一些公司正在发布他们所谓的“个人代理协议”。这是一个开放标准，旨在规定人工智能代理如何与企业交互。

paras.en: Enterprise AI startup Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, is part of the group. Taylor, who's also chairman of OpenAI and is leading the initiative, told CNBC in an interview that companies have a lot of work to do to figure out how and when personal agents are able to access information.
paras.zh: 由 Salesforce 前联合首席执行官布雷特·泰勒 (Bret Taylor) 联合创立的企业人工智能初创公司 Sierra 是该集团的一部分。泰勒也是 OpenAI 的董事长，也是该计划的领导者，他在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，公司还有很多工作要做，才能弄清楚个人代理如何以及何时能够访问信息。

paras.en: "Companies will know when it's a personal agent versus an actual person. For a lot of companies there's a risk: you don't want just a random bot that isn't acting on behalf of a person to have access to this service," Taylor said. “It is kind of chaos until such a standard exists."
paras.zh: “公司会知道什么时候是个人代理，什么时候是真人。对于很多公司来说，存在风险：你不希望只是一个不代表个人行事的随机机器人来访问这项服务，”泰勒说。 “在这样的标准存在之前，这会是一种混乱。”

paras.en: Meta's Muse has become the most popular and buzzy version of personal AI agents since hitting the market in early September. It soared to the top of Apple's App Store and remains there, ahead of ChatGPT. However, Amazon is among the companies that have blocked Meta's agents, citing worries of website scraping.
paras.zh: 自 9 月初上市以来，Meta 的 Muse 已成为最受欢迎和最热门的个人人工智能代理版本。它飙升至苹果应用商店的榜首，并保持领先地位，领先于 ChatGPT。然而，亚马逊是屏蔽 Meta 代理商的公司之一，理由是担心网站抓取。

paras.en: Amazon also blocked Perplexity's AI agent and sued the startup in November, alleging the company took steps to "conceal" its AI agents so they could continue to scrape Amazon's website without approval. Perplexity called the lawsuit a "bully tactic."
paras.zh: 亚马逊还屏蔽了 Perplexity 的人工智能代理，并于 11 月起诉这家初创公司，指控该公司采取措施“隐藏”其人工智能代理，以便他们可以在未经批准的情况下继续抓取亚马逊的网站。困惑称该诉讼为“欺凌策略”。

paras.en: For the new standard, Taylor compared it with the experience of logging into other websites with Google or Facebook credentials, technology he worked on when he was tech chief at Facebook. He said the practice will help with authentication so that businesses know if they're dealing with a bot, and will provide visibility into what personal agents are actually doing through these websites.
paras.zh: 对于新标准，泰勒将其与使用谷歌或 Facebook 凭据登录其他网站的体验进行了比较，这是他在担任 Facebook 技术主管时开发的技术。他表示，这种做法将有助于身份验证，以便企业知道他们是否正在与机器人打交道，并将提供个人代理通过这些网站实际执行的操作的可见性。

paras.en: David Singleton, vice president of engineering and consumer products at Meta Superintelligence Labs and former technology chief at Stripe, highlighted security. In order for agents to work well, he said, customers need to share credit card and personal information, and the new standard creates some level of visibility and control.
paras.zh: Meta Superintelligence Labs 工程和消费产品副总裁、Stripe 前技术主管 David Singleton 强调了安全性。他说，为了使代理能够顺利工作，客户需要共享信用卡和个人信息，而新标准创建了一定程度的可见性和控制。

paras.en: "We're defining rails that we hope personal agents and business agents can run over for the future," Singleton said, comparing it to email. "If you think about email, it works great because it is a standard that everyone can use to talk to each other, and we think this is going to be quite similar."
paras.zh: “我们正在定义我们希望个人代理和商业代理能够在未来运行的轨道，”辛格尔顿将其与电子邮件进行了比较。 “如果你想想电子邮件，它的效果很好，因为它是每个人都可以用来相互交谈的标准，我们认为这将非常相似。”

paras.en: Singleton said Muse already has millions of users in the U..S and it's "growing rapidly."
paras.zh: Singleton 表示，Muse 在美国已经拥有数百万用户，并且正在“快速增长”。

paras.en: "What we're finding is that people love using Muse for all kinds of things, things like signing their kids up for classes, finding and buying the best gifts, scheduling that dentist appointment that you have been putting off for six months," he said. "We need a mechanism to have it go faster and smoother."
paras.zh: “我们发现，人们喜欢用 Muse 做各种各样的事情，比如给孩子报名上课、寻找和购买最好的礼物、安排你已经推迟了六个月的牙医预约，”他说。 “我们需要一种机制，让事情进展得更快、更顺利。”

paras.en: While OpenAI and Anthropic aren't on board now, Taylor said he expects the AI giants to participate, and indicated he will be "really disappointed" if it's not being used by competitors.
paras.zh: 虽然 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 目前尚未加入，但泰勒表示，他预计人工智能巨头会参与其中，并表示如果竞争对手不使用它，他将“非常失望”。

paras.en: "The whole point of this is to be an open standard," Taylor said.
paras.zh: “这一切的重点是成为一个开放标准，”泰勒说。

articles.title: 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Francis Halzen for discovery of high-energy neutrinos

paras.en: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to Francis Halzen for “decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.” Halzen is a Belgium-born physicist, a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and principal investigator at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica.
paras.zh: 2026 年诺贝尔物理学奖授予弗朗西斯·哈尔岑 (Francis Halzen)，以表彰他“对冰立方中微子观测站和发现天体物理起源的高能中微子做出的决定性贡献”。哈尔岑是一位出生于比利时的物理学家，威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校教授，也是南极冰立方中微子观测站的首席研究员。

paras.en: “It’s a great pleasure to hear about this prize,” said Halzen during the press conference that followed the announcement. “I hope this reflects on the really courageous people who joined me in the beginning of this project.”
paras.zh: “很高兴听到这个奖项，”哈尔岑在宣布这一奖项后的新闻发布会上说道。 “我希望这能反映出在这个项目开始时加入我的那些真正勇敢的人。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “It’s very exciting,” says Michael H. Moloney, CEO of the American Institute of Physics. “It’s a timely and an important recognition of the extraordinary work that Dr. Halzen did to open up a whole new window on the universe.”
paras.zh: “这非常令人兴奋，”美国物理研究所首席执行官迈克尔·H·莫洛尼 (Michael H. Moloney) 说道。 “这是对哈尔岑博士为打开一扇了解宇宙的全新窗口所做的非凡工作的及时而重要的认可。”

paras.en: Indeed, IceCube—Halzen’s brainchild—gave humankind a fresh glimpse of the cosmos when it came online in 2010. Unlike the majority of the globe’s telescopes. which gather starlight, this unique observatory sees the universe via ghostly messengers called neutrinos. Combining the two has improved our understanding of some of the most distant and violent physical processes in the cosmos.
paras.zh: 事实上，哈尔岑的创意冰立方在 2010 年上线时让人类对宇宙有了新的认识。与全球大多数望远镜不同。这个独特的天文台聚集星光，通过称为中微子的幽灵信使来观察宇宙。将两者结合起来提高了我们对宇宙中一些最遥远、最剧烈的物理过程的理解。

paras.en: Neutrinos are the least understood of the 17 fundamental particles known to exist. They nearly always move through matter as if it isn’t there. So massive detectors are required to capture and study their exceedingly rare collisions with atoms.
paras.zh: 中微子是已知存在的 17 种基本粒子中我们了解最少的。它们几乎总是在物质中移动，就好像物质不存在一样。因此需要大型探测器来捕捉和研究它们与原子极其罕见的碰撞。

paras.en: IceCube does this with arrays of specialized sensors dispersed in the crystal-clear ice a mile beneath the surface of Antarctica. A high-energy neutrino, accelerated at the center of a faraway galaxy, will usually zip right through this subsurface deep freeze. But occasionally, it will hit an atom in a molecule of water ice, producing a shower of light that the sensors collect and use to reconstruct the neutrinos’ energies and directions of origin.
paras.zh: IceCube 通过分布在南极洲表面以下一英里的晶莹剔透的冰中的专用传感器阵列来实现这一点。高能中微子在遥远星系的中心加速，通常会直接穿过这个地下深度冻结。但偶尔，它会撞击水冰分子中的原子，产生一阵光，传感器收集这些光，并用它来重建中微子的能量和起源方向。

paras.en: After just a couple of years, IceCube confirmed it had measured the first high-energy neutrinos from beyond the solar system. Thanks in large part to IceCube, astronomers are heralding a new era of “multimessenger astronomy,” where neutrino measurements, traditional telescopes and gravitational-wave detectors together triangulate to pinpoint and scrutinize distant, obscure phenomena.
paras.zh: 仅仅几年后，IceCube 证实它已经测量到了来自太阳系以外的第一批高能中微子。在很大程度上要归功于 IceCube，天文学家预示着“多信使天文学”的新时代的到来，其中中微子测量、传统望远镜和引力波探测器一起进行三角测量，以精确定位和审查遥远、晦涩的现象。

paras.en: “People didn’t know that the extragalactic sources would be bright enough to be detected, so it was a risk,” says Jonathan Bagger, a theoretical physicist and CEO of the American Physical Society. “Halzen analyzed this subject and wrote proposals and got them through peer review—this was ultimately a testament to the system working.”
paras.zh: “人们不知道河外光源的亮度足以被探测到，所以这是一个风险，”理论物理学家兼美国物理学会首席执行官乔纳森·巴格尔（Jonathan Bagger）说。 “哈尔岑分析了这个主题并撰写了提案，并让它们通过了同行评审——这最终证明了该系统的运作。”

paras.en: The observatory is an ambitious and unprecedented feat of engineering. It was constructed by boring deep holes across a cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice using jets of hot water and then carefully lowering long strings of sensors into them. It remains the largest neutrino telescope in the world. This year’s Nobel therefore awards exactly the kind of modern, large-scale experimental science that is under financial threat in places like the U.S., where IceCube originated. (The Trump administration’s budget proposal for 2027 calls for halving IceCube’s funding.)
paras.zh: 天文台是一项雄心勃勃、前所未有的工程壮举。它是通过使用热水喷射在南极冰层上钻出一立方公里的深孔，然后小心地将一长串传感器放入其中而建造的。它仍然是世界上最大的中微子望远镜。因此，今年的诺贝尔奖授予的正是那种在 IceCube 的发源地美国等地面临财政威胁的现代大规模实验科学。 （特朗普政府的 2027 年预算提案要求将 IceCube 的资金减半。）

paras.en: “It’s big, publicly funded science,” Moloney says. “It shows that when we design audacious experiments, we can discover extraordinary things.”
paras.zh: “这是一项公共资助的大型科学，”莫洛尼说。 “这表明，当我们设计大胆的实验时，我们可以发现非凡的事物。”

paras.en: The Nobel Prize in Physics, first given in 1901, was previously awarded 119 times to a total of 229 individuals. Those recipients included Marie Curie, who was awarded in 1903 for making sense of radioactivity; Albert Einstein, who was awarded in 1921 for discovering how light and matter interact; I. I. Rabi, who was awarded in 1944 for discovering what would become the science behind magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); and Frederick Reines, who was awarded in 1995 for discovering low-energy neutrinos. Before Halzen’s win today, the last time the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to a single person was in 1992, when it went to French physicist Georges Charpak.
paras.zh: 诺贝尔物理学奖于 1901 年首次颁发，此前已颁发过 119 次，共有 229 人获奖。这些获奖者包括玛丽·居里 (Marie Curie)，她于 1903 年因对放射性的理解而获奖；阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦 (Albert Einstein)，1921 年因发现光与物质如何相互作用而获奖； I. I. Rabi，1944 年因发现磁共振成像 (MRI) 背后的科学而获奖；弗雷德里克·赖因斯 (Frederick Reines) 因发现低能中微子而于 1995 年获奖。在哈尔岑今天获奖之前，上一次将诺贝尔物理学奖授予个人是在 1992 年，当时的获奖者是法国物理学家乔治·查帕克 (Georges Charpak)。

paras.en: More recently, the physics Nobel Prize recognized a tool for studying the motion of electrons in 2023, the development of core techniques for building many of today’s artificial intelligence models in 2024, and the creation and study of weird quantum phenomena in macroscopic, handheld devices in 2025.
paras.zh: 最近，诺贝尔物理学奖表彰了 2023 年研究电子运动的工具、2024 年开发用于构建当今许多人工智能模型的核心技术以及 2025 年在宏观手持设备中创建和研究奇怪量子现象的工具。

paras.en: The prize will be presented in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel’s death.
paras.zh: 该奖项将于 12 月 10 日阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔逝世周年纪念日在斯德哥尔摩颁奖。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (10/6/26): This is a breaking news story and will be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（10/6/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，将会更新。

articles.title: What makes a good AI safety test? Experts explain why even the best techniques may not be powerful enough

paras.en: Artificial intelligence agents keep turning up in places they’re not meant to be. In June an experimental OpenAI model gained unauthorized access to nonpublic files on a Australian government website for the nation’s Medicare program. Researchers have since found signs of suspected AI agents probing Library and Archives Canada, while another investigation linked OpenAI agents to more than 16,000 scans of a United Nations statistics service.
paras.zh: 人工智能代理不断出现在他们不应该出现的地方。 6 月，一个实验性 OpenAI 模型未经授权访问了澳大利亚政府网站上的国家医疗保险计划的非公开文件。此后，研究人员发现了可疑 AI 代理对加拿大图书馆和档案馆进行探测的迹象，而另一项调查则将 OpenAI 代理与联合国统计服务的 16,000 多次扫描联系起来。

paras.en: Still more examples are coming from inside the AI firms. OpenAI recently disclosed six cases of concerning model behavior, and Anthropic has also admitted its models gained unauthorized access to three organizations’ systems during testing.
paras.zh: 还有更多例子来自人工智能公司内部。 OpenAI 最近披露了六起有关模型行为的案例，Anthropic 也承认其模型在测试过程中未经授权访问了三个组织的系统。

paras.en: In fact, all of these incidents happened during testing. At the same time, the AI agents seem to know they are being watched during these tests—and they can cover their tracks. That’s why some experts—including Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive officer—say we need better tests to ensure AI operates in a way we feel comfortable with.
paras.zh: 事实上，所有这些事件都发生在测试过程中。与此同时，人工智能代理似乎知道他们在这些测试期间受到监视，并且他们可以掩盖自己的踪迹。这就是为什么一些专家（包括 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪）表示，我们需要更好的测试，以确保人工智能以我们感觉舒服的方式运行。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: This problem is often referred to as one of “alignment” by AI firms and researchers in the field. A “misaligned” model is an unsafe or rogue model.
paras.zh: 这个问题通常被人工智能公司和该领域的研究人员称为“对齐”问题之一。 “错位”模型是不安全或流氓模型。

paras.en: “Right now we test the finished model from the outside right before release,” says Marius Hobbhahn. “That doesn’t work in studying alignment, especially as misalignment, [evaluation] awareness and other related maladies persist.” Hobbhahn is chief executive officer and founder of Apollo Research, an AI safety organization that works with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind to test their models for risk.
paras.zh: “现在我们在发布之前从外部测试成品模型，”Marius Hobbhahn 说。 “这对于研究一致性是行不通的，尤其是在偏差、[评估]意识和其他相关弊病持续存在的情况下。” Hobbhahn 是 Apollo Research 的首席执行官兼创始人，Apollo Research 是一家人工智能安全组织，与 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google DeepMind 合作测试他们的模型的风险。

paras.en: Hobbhahn adds that current standards for safety testing are inadequate. “I think without embedded evaluations, we should place very little confidence in current safety results,” he says.
paras.zh: 霍布哈恩补充说，目前的安全测试标准还不够。 “我认为，如果没有嵌入式评估，我们对当前的安全结果应该没有信心，”他说。

paras.en: But changing when and where models are tested isn’t simple. Before you can design a test, you must decide what counts as a passing grade—and that’s not obvious.
paras.zh: 但改变模型测试的时间和地点并不简单。在设计测试之前，您必须决定什么才算及格——而这并不明显。

paras.en: “The problem we have about coming up with the ideal test is: we need to know what perfect alignment looks like—as in what good looks like—and unfortunately we do not have a good theory for that yet,” says Jack Hopkins, an independent AI safety researcher in London, who previously worked at Anthropic.
paras.zh: “我们在提出理想测试时遇到的问题是：我们需要知道完美的对齐是什么样子的——就像好的样子一样——但不幸的是，我们还没有一个好的理论，”伦敦的独立人工智能安全研究员、曾在 Anthropic 工作过的杰克·霍普金斯 (Jack Hopkins) 说。

paras.en: Different people have different opinions about what is and isn’t acceptable, safe behavior for an AI model. And even where there is consensus—the idea that models shouldn’t deceive users or misrepresent what they’re doing, for instance—it can be difficult to pin down what that means in practice.
paras.zh: 对于人工智能模型什么是可接受的、什么是不可接受的安全行为，不同的人有不同的看法。即使存在共识——例如模型不应该欺骗用户或歪曲他们正在做的事情——也很难确定这在实践中意味着什么。

paras.en: “It’s really hard to catch all [the] ways in which a model could deceive you because it itself doesn’t know necessarily that it’s deceiving you,” Hopkins says.
paras.zh: 霍普金斯说：“要找出模型欺骗你的所有方式真的很难，因为它本身并不一定知道它在欺骗你。”

paras.en: Hobbhahn agrees. “With today’s science, we usually can’t show with high confidence that dangerous behavior isn’t there,” he says. “What we can say is, ‘We tried hard to find it and failed.’ This is a problem.”
paras.zh: 霍巴恩同意这一点。 “以当今的科学水平，我们通常无法高度确信不存在危险行为，”他说。 “我们能说的是，‘我们努力寻找它，但失败了。’这是一个问题。”

paras.en: Still, to be able to identify safety issues and head them off before they appear, the field desperately needs better tests. Hobbhahn suggests that evaluations should run alongside a model’s development, examining the training process itself—including how models are rewarded and what behavior they produce along the way.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，为了能够识别安全问题并在其出现之前阻止它们，该领域迫切需要更好的测试。 Hobbhahn 建议评估应该与模型的开发同时进行，检查训练过程本身，包括模型如何获得奖励以及模型在此过程中产生什么行为。

paras.en: That would mean testing models at different checkpoints during training rather than testing a close-to-final version. Researchers would also have to make sure the tests actually work. One way of doing that is to run them against models that researchers already know are misaligned: if the test can’t spot the problems in a known model, Hobbhahn argues, there’s little reason to believe it might do better on a new one.
paras.zh: 这意味着在训练期间在不同的检查点测试模型，而不是测试接近最终的版本。研究人员还必须确保测试确实有效。一种方法是将它们与研究人员已知存在偏差的模型进行对比：霍布哈恩认为，如果测试无法发现已知模型中的问题，就没有理由相信它在新模型上可能会做得更好。

paras.en: Testing should continue once models are being used internally, too—and include any attempts to find ways around whatever monitoring systems are supposed to catch bad actors. Hobbhahn says independent evaluators should be given employee-level access to carry out that work rather than probing a largely finished system from the outside. The results of these tests, he says, should then be published.
paras.zh: 一旦模型在内部使用，测试也应该继续进行，并包括寻找绕过任何监控系统来捕获不良行为者的方法的尝试。霍布哈恩表示，独立评估人员应该获得员工级别的访问权限来开展这项工作，而不是从外部探索一个基本完成的系统。他说，这些测试的结果应该随后公布。

paras.en: But even the best tests might not be good enough, Hopkins reckons, because models are always shifting capabilities.
paras.zh: 但霍普金斯认为，即使是最好的测试也可能不够好，因为模型总是在改变能力。

paras.en: “I think what we can do is get arbitrarily close to” perfect when it comes to testing, he says. “But the problem of only getting arbitrarily close and leaving this little space where the model can act in line with the letter of the law but not in the spirit [of it] is that if the model gets really smart and really powerful, the effective impact of that tiny gap gets amplified.”
paras.zh: 他说，“我认为我们能做的就是在测试方面任意接近”完美。 “但是，仅仅随意接近并留下这个小空间，模型可以按照法律条文行事，但不符合其精神，问题是，如果模型变得非常聪明和非常强大，那么这个微小差距的有效影响就会被放大。”

articles.title: Two meteor showers are lighting up the October sky—here’s how to see them

paras.en: It’s fall, which means the nights are getting colder and longer—but they will also soon be speckled with shooting stars when a pair of meteor showers make their annual visit to Earth this month.
paras.zh: 现在是秋天，这意味着夜晚变得越来越冷、越来越长，但当一对流星雨本月访问地球时，它们很快就会布满流星。

paras.en: The first is the Draconid meteor shower, which is expected to peak on the night of October 8, followed by the Orionid meteor shower, which will peak on October 21, according to NASA.
paras.zh: 据美国宇航局称，第一个是天龙座流星雨，预计将在 10 月 8 日晚上达到峰值，其次是猎户座流星雨，将在 10 月 21 日达到峰值。

paras.en: The Draconids and Orionids are basically cosmic leftovers: As comets or asteroids orbit the sun, they leave a trail of debris, dust and ice. When Earth crosses paths with these trails, bits of that material burn up in the planet’s atmosphere—producing the stunning streaks of light we call meteors, or shooting stars.
paras.zh: 天龙座流星雨和猎户座流星雨基本上是宇宙的残余物：当彗星或小行星绕太阳运行时，它们会留下碎片、灰尘和冰的痕迹。当地球与这些轨迹交叉时，这些物质的碎片会在地球的大气层中燃烧，产生令人惊叹的光条纹，我们称之为流星或流星。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The Draconids—which are named for the constellation Draco—owe themselves to Comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, a space rock that is just 1.24 miles (about two kilometers) in diameter. The Orionids—which are similarly named for the constellation Orion—originate from Halley’s Comet, which is about 9.3 miles (15 kilometers) in diameter at its widest.
paras.zh: 天龙座流星雨——以天龙座命名——归功于彗星 21P/Giacobini-Zinner，这是一颗直径仅为 1.24 英里（约两公里）的太空岩石。猎户座流星雨——以猎户座命名——起​​源于哈雷彗星，其最宽直径约为 9.3 英里（15 公里）。

paras.en: The Draconids are the smaller shower, and NASA expects the display to only produce “a few meteors per hour” this year. On the upside, you don’t need to stay awake until the wee hours of the night to see it: “This is an ideal meteor shower for casual sky watchers, since it begins soon after darkness falls rather than in the early morning hours,” the agency says.
paras.zh: 天龙座流星雨是较小的流星雨，美国宇航局预计今年的流星雨只会产生“每小时几颗流星”。从好的方面来说，你不需要熬夜到凌晨才能看到它：“对于休闲天空观察者来说，这是一场理想的流星雨，因为它在夜幕降临后不久而不是凌晨开始，”该机构表示。

paras.en: Sky gazers might have more luck spotting a meteor during the Orionids’ peak on October 21, but the “prime viewing window” will be before dawn, after the moon sets, according to NASA.
paras.zh: 据美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 称，在 10 月 21 日猎户座流星雨高峰期间，天空观测者可能会更幸运地发现流星，但“最佳观测窗口”将在黎明之前、月亮落下之后。

paras.en: As with any meteor shower, you’ll have your best chance of catching shooting stars by viewing the sky from an area with limited light pollution and giving your eyes about 30 minutes to adjust to the dark.
paras.zh: 与任何流星雨一样，您最好在光污染有限的区域观看天空，并给您的眼睛大约 30 分钟的时间来适应黑暗，从而获得捕捉流星的最佳机会。

paras.en: If you miss these two showers, know that they aren’t all the sky has to offer this fall. As Scientific American previously reported, two other showers, the Southern and Northern Taurids, are set to peak on the nights of November 4–5 and 11–12, respectively. Happy viewing!
paras.zh: 如果您错过了这两场阵雨，请知道它们并不是今年秋天天空所提供的全部。正如《科学美国人》之前报道的那样，另外两场流星雨，南金牛座流星雨和北金牛座流星雨，预计分别在 11 月 4 日至 5 日和 11 月 11 日至 12 日夜间达到峰值。观看愉快！

articles.title: Your voice is more than sound. It’s part of who you are
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Meet Jules Rodriguez. He’s a dad, husband, former science teacher, podcaster and stand-up comedian — someone who has always had a lot to say.
paras.zh: 认识朱尔斯·罗德里格斯。他是一位父亲、丈夫、前科学老师、播客和单口喜剧演员——一个总是有很多话要说的人。

paras.en: But ALS has taken away his ability to speak. Now, Jules communicates by typing with his eyes, and an AI-generated voice clone speaks his words aloud.
paras.zh: 但肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）已经剥夺了他说话的能力。现在，朱尔斯通过眼睛打字进行交流，人工智能生成的语音克隆会大声说出他的话。

paras.en: In this episode of The Deep End, hear Jules’ story, as well as perspectives from scientists and clinicians on why a voice is so much more than a way to communicate. Human brains are poised to seek out voices, and all the various kinds of information they can hold.
paras.zh: 在这一集中的《The Deep End》中，聆听朱尔斯的故事，以及科学家和临床医生对为什么声音不仅仅是一种交流方式的看法。人类的大脑随时准备寻找声音以及它们所能容纳的各种信息。

paras.en: Jules’ experience reveals just how much of our identity is created by the way we sound — and what it means when that sound disappears.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯的经历揭示了我们的身份在多大程度上是由我们发声的方式决定的——以及当声音消失时意味着什么。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: Jules Rodriguez has always had a lot to say. He has talked to kids as their science teacher. He’s talked about his life for years on a podcast he created with his wife.
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：朱尔斯·罗德里格斯总是有很多话要说。他作为孩子们的科学老师与他们交谈。多年来，他一直在与妻子共同创建的播客中谈论自己的生活。

paras.en: Jules: Hey everyone, it’s been a while and I am so excited to be back.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：大家好，已经有一段时间了，我很高兴能回来。

paras.en: Sanders: He even does some of the most terrifying talking I can imagine. He performs in front of crowds as a stand-up comedian.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他甚至说了一些我能想象到的最可怕的言论。他作为一名单口喜剧演员在人群面前表演。

paras.en: Jules: I have to pick my battles. Do I want to be right or do I want to eat tonight?
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我必须选择我的战斗。我想要是对的还是我今晚想吃东西？

paras.en: Sanders: His wife, Maria Aleandra Fernandez, who goes by MA, says that Jules’ voice is one of her very favorites.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的妻子玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯（Maria Aleandra Fernandez）（简称 MA）说朱尔斯的声音是她最喜欢的声音之一。

paras.en: MA: Oh man, I definitely love hearing Jules’ voice. I’m not just saying that, but I do.
paras.zh: MA：天啊，我真的很喜欢听朱尔斯的声音。我不仅这么说，而且确实这么做了。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules was born and raised in Miami. He and MA have a nine-year-old son named Skyler. Jules loves baseball. He loves the Marlins. He loves being outside. He loves action.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯在迈阿密出生和长大。他和马云有一个九岁的儿子，名叫斯凯勒。朱尔斯喜欢棒球。他喜欢马林鱼队。他喜欢呆在外面。他热爱行动。

paras.en: Jules: I was always pretty high energy. I loved mountain biking, snorkeling, fishing, and playing all sports, really. Baseball is my favorite sport to play and watch.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我总是精力充沛。我真的很喜欢山地自行车、浮潜、钓鱼以及所有运动。棒球是我最喜欢玩和观看的运动。

paras.en: Sanders: The night Jules and MA met, they were doing karaoke at her 30th birthday party.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯和妈妈见面的那天晚上，他们正在她 30 岁生日聚会上唱卡拉 OK。

paras.en: MA: A friend introduced us, and it was kind of a, sort of a love at first sight situation. We danced, we sang.
paras.zh: MA：一位朋友介绍我们认识的，这是一种一见钟情的情况。我们跳舞，我们唱歌。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules’ karaoke song choice was a classic that no millennial can resist. It was Sir Mix-A-Lot’s “Baby Got Back.”
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯选择的卡拉 OK 歌曲是千禧一代无法抗拒的经典之作。这是 Mix-A-Lot 爵士的《宝贝回来了》。

paras.en: MA: “Baby Got Back,” yeah. That one he got up there and sang with a couple of his friends. It was like him and his three other buddies that were there with him. And oh, that was just so joyous. And we had karaoke at our wedding as well, so, we’ve always loved to sing, to dance. We took ballroom dancing classes. We, like, danced at every wedding. All of it. So, yeah.
paras.zh: MA：“宝贝回来了”，是的。他站在那里和他的几个朋友一起唱歌。就像他和他的另外三个伙伴一样。哦，那真是太令人高兴了。我们的婚礼上也唱卡拉OK，所以，我们一直喜欢唱歌、跳舞。我们参加了交谊舞课程。我们就像在每次婚礼上跳舞一样。所有这一切。所以，是的。

paras.en: Sanders: One more thing about Jules. He has ALS. That’s short for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a disease also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease or motor neuron disease. Jules has lived with ALS since 2020. Many of his muscles no longer respond to his brain’s signals, which means he can’t move his body or breathe on his own. This dropped signal between brain and body also means that Jules is no longer able to talk. That line you heard earlier from Jules?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于朱尔斯的另一件事。他患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症。这是肌萎缩侧索硬化症的缩写，这种疾病也称为卢伽雷氏病或运动神经元病。 Jules 自 2020 年以来一直患有 ALS。他的许多肌肉不再对大脑的信号做出反应，这意味着他无法移动身体或自行呼吸。大脑和身体之间的信号丢失也意味着朱尔斯无法再说话。你之前从朱尔斯那里听到过这句话吗？

paras.en: Sanders: That was an AI-generated, synthetic voice speaking his words. His voice, as it used to exist, is gone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是人工智能生成的合成声音，说出了他的话。他的声音，就像以前那样，已经消失了。

paras.en: Welcome to Season 2 of The Deep End, a podcast about our brains and ourselves. I’m your host, Laura Sanders, a reporter with Science News. And this season, called Talk to Me, is about the human voice.
paras.zh: 欢迎来到《The Deep End》第二季，这是一个关于我们的大脑和我们自己的播客。我是主持人劳拉·桑德斯 (Laura Sanders)，是《科学新闻》的记者。这一季名为《跟我说话》，讲述的是人类的声音。

paras.en: [intro] Hey Mom, can I tell you something? The casual observer sees little of the vigorous activity at the site of voice production. The voice is absolutely an integral part of your identity. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [简介] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？不经意的观察者几乎看不到声音产生处的剧烈活动。声音绝对是您身份的一个组成部分。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: [voice] My poor little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin but by the content of their character. I have a dream…
paras.zh: [声音]我可怜的孩子们有一天会生活在一个国家，在那里他们将不会根据他们的肤色而是根据他们的性格内容来评判。我有一个梦想…

paras.en: Sanders: Voices can be powerful. We save and replay voicemails.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音是有力量的。我们保存并重播语音邮件。

paras.en: [voice] Hey, dude, I’m just calling to say hi and chit-chat.
paras.zh: [声音]嘿，伙计，我打电话只是想打个招呼，聊聊。

paras.en: Sanders: We call someone special just to hear their voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们打电话给特别的人只是为了听听他们的声音。

paras.en: Sanders: We love to hear people tell stories.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们喜欢听人们讲故事。

paras.en: Sanders: But why? What is it inside these voices that can calm us down or terrify us or have us laughing so hard we’re gasping for air? In this season, we’re going to explore a simple but deep question. What gives the human voice so much power? You’re going to hear all sorts of voices. They’ll tell a story of what connects us and what happens when those connections are lost. Over the next six episodes, we’ll explore a new digital world. In this world, human voices no longer need a human body to create them. You’ll hear how machines can speak for those who can’t, and even pull words from the brains of people who can’t speak. It’s a story about how technology is changing the human voice in ways that are good, bad, and fascinating. Let’s begin.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是为什么呢？这些声音里到底有什么东西可以让我们平静下来，或者让我们感到恐惧，或者让我们笑得喘不过气来？本季，我们将探讨一个简单而深刻的问题。是什么赋予人类声音如此强大的力量？你会听到各种各样的声音。他们将讲述一个故事，讲述是什么将我们联系在一起，以及当这些联系消失时会发生什么。在接下来的六集中，我们将探索一个新的数字世界。在这个世界上，人类的声音不再需要人体来创造。你会听到机器如何为那些不会说话的人说话，甚至从不会说话的人的大脑中提取单词。这是一个关于技术如何以好的、坏的和令人着迷的方式改变人类声音的故事。让我们开始吧。

paras.en: Sanders: People listen for voices in everything. There’s a parallel you might have heard of. It’s a weird quirk of human brains that we’re able to find faces everywhere, too. That’s why you’ve seen the shape of a face in an electrical outlet or a car grill or a random pattern on the wall. Our brains love seeing faces. And it turns out our brains love hearing voices too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人们在一切事情上都会倾听声音。您可能听说过一个类似的情况。我们也能够在任何地方找到面孔，这也是人类大脑的一个奇怪的怪癖。这就是为什么你会在电源插座或汽车烤架上看到一张脸的形状，或者在墙上看到随机的图案。我们的大脑喜欢看到面孔。事实证明我们的大脑也喜欢听声音。

paras.en: Greg Bryant: It’s really well established that there’s a voice-selective region and it’s activated really early.
paras.zh: 格雷格·布莱恩特：确实存在一个声音选择区域，而且它很早就被激活了。

paras.en: Sanders: Greg Bryant is a cognitive scientist who studies vocal communications at UCLA. He tells me that there’s a spot in the brain that responds strongly to voices.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：格雷格·布莱恩特是一位认知科学家，在加州大学洛杉矶分校研究声音交流。他告诉我，大脑中有一个地方对声音反应强烈。

paras.en: Bryant: Yeah, we hear voices in all kinds of stuff. I mean, you ever been out camping and you’re like [whispers], you know, or something, you know, you hear like whispering. And yeah, it’s really easy to hallucinate a voice.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：是的，我们听到各种各样的声音。我的意思是，你曾经出去露营，你就像[窃窃私语]，你知道，或者什么，你知道，你听到像窃窃私语。是的，我们很容易产生幻觉。

paras.en: Sanders: Part of the reason our brains tune into voices might be that they are packed with information, information that goes well beyond words.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们的大脑适应声音的部分原因可能是它们充满了信息，这些信息远远超出了语言的范围。

paras.en: Bryant: It’s definitely a very intimate entryway to a person because you get emotion, history, your body, all in one quick auditory signal. So I think it’s very personal. It gives you access to a person’s individual nature. And it contains language and vocal emotions in a way that’s very direct and evocative. It’s one of the most personal things that you encounter with another person.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：这绝对是一个人的非常亲密的入口，因为你可以通过一个快速的听觉信号获得情感、历史、你的身体。所以我认为这是非常个人化的。它使您可以了解一个人的个性。它以一种非常直接和令人回味的方式包含语言和声音情感。这是你与另一个人遇到的最私人的事情之一。

paras.en: Sanders: Voices are also some of the first social inputs a baby gets.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音也是婴儿获得的第一个社交输入。

paras.en: Sanders: In utero, a baby hears a mother’s voice all day, singing to the radio, ordering a smoothie, talking to coworkers. This voice, carried on waves through the amniotic fluid, makes a big impression.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在子宫里，婴儿整天都会听到母亲的声音，对着收音机唱歌，点一杯冰沙，与同事交谈。这种声音通过羊水以波的形式传播，给人留下了深刻的印象。

paras.en: Bryant: Kids hear voices actually before they’re even born. That’s one of the most salient auditory stimuli in utero, right? That they know their mother’s voice before they’re even born, and even have picked up aspects of the rhythm and the language they speak before they’re born. So it’s just something the brain is just attracted to right from the beginning of development. Because I think it’s such an important source of information about the people around you and what’s happening.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：孩子们在出生之前就已经听到了声音。这是子宫内最显着的听觉刺激之一，对吧？他们甚至在出生之前就知道母亲的声音，甚至在出生之前就已经掌握了母亲所说的节奏和语言的某些方面。所以这只是大脑从发育之初就被吸引的东西。因为我认为这是关于你周围的人和正在发生的事情的重要信息来源。

paras.en: Sanders: People’s voices are both extremely common and at the same time special and unique. So when people are faced with the prospect of losing their voice, which is what happens to most people with ALS, including Jules, they’re looking at a profound loss.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人们的声音既极其普遍，同时又特殊且独特。因此，当人们面临失去声音的前景时，这就是大多数肌萎缩侧索硬化症患者（包括朱尔斯）都会发生的情况，他们面临着巨大的损失。

paras.en: Kate Nilson: So much. So much is in a voice.
paras.zh: 凯特·尼尔森：就这么多。声音里蕴藏着如此多的内容。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech-language pathologist Kate Nilson. She works with people who anticipate that they will lose the ability to talk, including people with ALS. She uses lots of tools to help people plan for this eventuality. That includes recording messages for use later on and banking their voice, a method that allows typed words to be spoken by a computer program. In recent years, her job has expanded as she works with people to create fancy AI-powered voice clones.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是言语病理学家凯特·尼尔森。她与那些预计自己将失去说话能力的人一起工作，其中包括肌萎缩侧索硬化症患者。她使用许多工具来帮助人们为这种可能性做好计划。这包括录制消息以供以后使用以及存储他们的声音，这是一种允许计算机程序说出键入的单词的方法。近年来，她的工作范围不断扩大，她与人们合作创建由人工智能驱动的精美语音克隆。

paras.en: Nilson: When I am a clinician in the clinic and someone has just gotten the diagnosis, they’re oftentimes told that there’s not a lot they can do, right? There’s not a lot of treatments out there. We’re working on it, but there’s not a lot of treatments currently. There’s no exercises to make you stronger. This is something they can do. So a lot of times, I can do this. This is something that I can do to be proactive and to be ready for the future. So there’s that.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：当我是诊所的临床医生并且有人刚刚得到诊断时，他们经常被告知他们无能为力，对吧？那里没有太多的治疗方法。我们正在研究这个问题，但目前还没有很多治疗方法。没有任何练习可以让你变得更强壮。这是他们可以做的事情。所以很多时候，我都能做到这一点。这是我可以采取的积极主动并为未来做好准备的事情。就是这样。

paras.en: Sanders: Nilson’s perspective means that she sees up close and personal the meaning and the importance of a person’s voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：尼尔森的视角意味着她能够近距离地、个人地看到一个人声音的意义和重要性。

paras.en: Nilson: There’s also thinking that these messages, these voices, can be saved by the family forever. And so that means a lot to people. But most importantly, what is really hard until you’re in it is how much your voice is you.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：还有人认为这些信息、这些声音可以被家人永远保存。所以这对人们来说意义重大。但最重要的是，在你真正融入其中之前，真正困难的是你的声音在多大程度上是你自己。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules uses an assistive device that lets him type by looking at letters and words on a screen. His synthetic voice then reads what he has just typed with his eyes. For this story, I also interviewed a man named Patrick Darling, who communicates with typed words and a voice clone that speaks them. Patrick is 33 and lives in Bristol, England.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯使用一种辅助设备，让他通过查看屏幕上的字母和单词来打字。然后他的合成声音会用眼睛读出他刚刚输入的内容。在这个故事中，我还采访了一位名叫帕特里克·达林（Patrick Darling）的人，他通过打字和说话的语音克隆进行交流。帕特里克 (Patrick) 33 岁，住在英国布里斯托尔。

paras.en: Patrick Darling: I’ve been a barista, a barber, boatman, a gamer, a painter, a voice actor, Youtube content creator and a musician.
paras.zh: Patrick Darling：我做过咖啡师、理发师、船夫、游戏玩家、画家、配音演员、Youtube 内容创作者和音乐家。

paras.en: Sanders: Patrick was diagnosed with ALS in 2022. Since then, the disease has taken a lot from him, including his voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：帕特里克于 2022 年被诊断出患有 ALS。从那时起，这种疾病就夺走了他的很多东西，包括他的声音。

paras.en: Patrick: Now four years later, I have lost the ability to sing and play my instruments.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：四年过去了，我已经失去了唱歌和演奏乐器的能力。

paras.en: Patrick: Being unable to talk is extremely isolating, unbelievably frustrating and oftentimes frightening. I think people who don’t really know you often feel uncomfortable by your silence and I think it’s easy for people to forget that there is still a person stuck in there.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：无法说话是一种极度孤立、令人难以置信的沮丧，而且常常令人恐惧。我认为那些不太了解你的人常常会对你的沉默感到不舒服，而且我认为人们很容易忘记还有一个人被困在那里。

paras.en: Sanders: Patrick’s description of feeling forgotten, of the isolation and fear that comes from not being able to talk, came up again and again as I reported this story. To step back here, the loss of a voice is one loss of many. ALS progresses differently for everyone, but its hallmark is a loss of movement. The disease interrupts the signals from the brain to the muscles, meaning that people lose the ability to button a shirt or apply their mascara or walk. How scary, how frustrating, how deeply annoying it must be to not be able to move in the ways you need. As I’m talking to Jules and MA on a video call, there are a few times this hits home. For instance, when a gnat starts circling Jules.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：帕特里克描述的被遗忘的感觉、无法说话所带来的孤立和恐惧，在我报道这个故事时一次又一次地出现。退一步讲，失去声音是许多人的损失之一。每个人的 ALS 进展情况都不同，但其特点是运动能力丧失。这种疾病会中断从大脑到肌肉的信号，这意味着人们无法扣衬衫、涂睫毛膏或走路。无法按照你需要的方式行动，这是多么可怕、多么令人沮丧、多么令人烦恼。当我在视频通话中与朱尔斯和马云交谈时，有几次这句话击中了我的要害。例如，当一只蚊子开始围着朱尔斯转时。

paras.en: MA: He has a little fly flying around. Can you imagine not being able to swat away a gnat? Yeah. Torture chamber. Yeah.
paras.zh: MA：他有一只小苍蝇在飞来飞去。你能想象无法赶走一只蚊子吗？是的。酷刑室。是的。

paras.en: Sanders: On top of not being able to swat the gnat, if Jules didn’t have a way to communicate, he couldn’t even ask MA to swat the gnat for him. He couldn’t say he’s annoyed or thirsty or that he’s getting pinched by something. He couldn’t ask her to turn off whatever machine is beeping and driving him crazy. It’s hard to imagine. In a class Kate Nilson teaches at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, she asks her students, who are all future speech pathologists, to experience a tiny sliver of what it must feel like to not talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：除了无法拍掉蚊子之外，如果朱尔斯没有办法沟通，他甚至无法要求妈妈帮他拍掉蚊子。他不能说自己生气、口渴，或者被什么东西夹住了。他不能要求她关掉任何发出嘟嘟声、让他发疯的机器。很难想象。凯特·尼尔森 (Kate Nilson) 在明尼苏达大学双城分校 (University of Minnesota Twin Cities) 教授的一堂课上，她要求她的学生（他们都是未来的语言病理学家）体验一下不说话的感觉。

paras.en: Nilson: One of the assignments that I assign to my class is that they have to put an app on their phone and they can’t talk for two hours. They have to go for two hours not talking, but only using an app on their phone just to get that experience of what that is like.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：我给班级布置的作业之一是，他们必须在手机上安装一个应用程序，并且两个小时内不能说话。他们必须花两个小时不说话，只使用手机上的应用程序，才能体验到那种感觉。

paras.en: Sanders: When they wanted to say something, Nielsen’s students used their phones to type the words, and then a robotic voice read them aloud. They told her that during the exercise, they stopped trying to say what they were thinking as much, and how lonely that felt.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当他们想说些什么时，尼尔森的学生用手机输入单词，然后机器人声音大声朗读它们。他们告诉她，在练习过程中，他们不再试图说出自己的想法，以及那种感觉是多么孤独。

paras.en: Nilson: And here these are, you know, 24-year-old speech pathology grad students, and so many of them in their reflection back to me say, “I didn’t realize how much my voice is who I am.”
paras.zh: 尼尔森：你知道，这些都是 24 岁的言语病理学研究生，他们中的许多人在向我反映时说，“我没有意识到我的声音在多大程度上代表了我自己。”

paras.en: Sanders: They had things to say, but they didn’t, because of the time and the effort it would take.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们有话要说，但他们没有说，因为这需要时间和精力。

paras.en: Nilson: If anyone listening is curious, I would just encourage you to try that. And then you see what that is like and what it feels like to have so much to say and not be able to say it, and what that takes away from your personality and who you are. And not even not being able to say it, but not being able to say it in your voice. It’s so much who we are that it’s, it’s hard to explain. It’s more of a feeling. But it’s a big one.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：如果有人好奇，我会鼓励你尝试一下。然后你就会明白那是什么感觉，有那么多话要说却又无法说出来是什么感觉，以及这会剥夺你的个性和你是谁。甚至不是不能说出来，而是不能用你的声音说出来。我们是谁，很难解释。这更多的是一种感觉。但这是一件大事。

paras.en: Sanders: I did her assignment too. I’ll come clean here and say that I procrastinated a lot. There was never a good day for me to not talk. I had to lead a meeting. I was coaching soccer. And that, in and of itself, is informative because it tells me just how important my voice is to me. So I finally got around to it. It was hard. I used a straightforward, no bells and whistles app on my phone. I typed words and then a pleasant but quite robotic woman’s voice named Samantha in the app spoke them aloud for me as I went through my day.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我也完成了她的任务。我会在这里坦白说我拖延了很多。对我来说，没有一天是不说话的好日子。我必须主持一次会议。我当时正在教足球。这本身就具有丰富的信息，因为它告诉我我的声音对我来说有多重要。所以我终于抽出时间来做这件事。这很难。我在手机上使用了一个简单、没有花里胡哨的应用程序。我输入文字，然后应用程序中一个名叫萨曼莎（Samantha）的愉快但相当机器人的女人的声音在我度过这一天时为我大声朗读它们。

paras.en: [voice] Would you like cereal for breakfast? What kind? Cheerios? Honey Nut Crunch?
paras.zh: [声音] 早餐想吃麦片吗？什么样的？麦片？蜂蜜坚果脆饼？

paras.en: Sanders: The logistical stuff was tricky, especially for a rushed morning.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：后勤工作很棘手，尤其是在一个匆忙的早晨。

paras.en: [voice]: Did you brush your teeth? Daddy will drive you to school. He is leaving in five minutes.
paras.zh: [声音]：你刷牙了吗？爸爸会开车送你去学校。他五分钟后就要离开。

paras.en: Sanders: I couldn’t call the cats inside. Listen.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我无法叫里面的猫。听。

paras.en: [voice] Here, kitty, kitty, kitty. Come on. Bonnie, Arlo, here, kitty, kitty, kitty.
paras.zh: [声音] 在这里，小猫，小猫，小猫。快点。邦妮，阿洛，在这里，小猫，小猫，小猫。

paras.en: Sanders: But what was harder, I realized later, were the moments I couldn’t or didn’t connect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但后来我意识到，更困难的是我无法或无法联系的时刻。

paras.en: Sanders: It was hard to ask my kids if they had any dreams the night before.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很难问我的孩子们前一天晚上是否做了梦。

paras.en: Sanders: I couldn’t say a quick hello to a friend at the gym. Instead, I smiled extra big at her and felt pretty awkward about it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我无法在健身房与朋友快速打招呼。相反，我对她笑得很开心，并感到很尴尬。

paras.en: Sanders: I understood a bit more about what Patrick meant about feeling isolated. I stopped trying to connect. I self-censored. I didn’t have to stop. After all, I had the technology to communicate in my literal hand, but it felt too hard, too slow, too artificial. It didn’t feel like it was worth the effort for me to type and to ask other people to slow down and listen. My brief experiment gave me a glimpse, a tiny glimpse, into a life without a voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我对帕特里克感到孤立的含义有了更多的了解。我停止尝试连接。我自我审查。我不必停下来。毕竟，我拥有可以用我的双手进行交流的技术，但感觉太难、太慢、太人工。我觉得不值得我费力打字并要求其他人放慢速度倾听。我短暂的实验让我瞥见了一个没有声音的生活。

paras.en: Piotrowski: Being able to ask for things, being able to tell someone when you are in pain. Or when you’re feeling good, or when something that they do is helpful.
paras.zh: Piotrowski：能够提出请求，能够在痛苦时告诉别人。或者当你感觉良好时，或者当他们做的事情有帮助时。

paras.en: Sanders: Speech-language pathologist Jessica Piotrowski works at the UC Davis Center for Voice and Swallowing. She helps people who are losing their ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：言语病理学家杰西卡·皮奥特罗斯基在加州大学戴维斯分校声音和吞咽中心工作。她帮助那些失去说话能力的人。

paras.en: Pietrowski: The interesting thing that I have learned in working in this field, and I’m not sure if the general public is aware, is that for many of these individuals, losing their speech is way more devastating than losing their mobility. You know, you think you think about what these individuals often are unfortunately losing: their mobility, their independence, their swallowing. But being able to communicate is going to, in some way, help them a little bit through all those things. And going through all of those changes without a voice or a way to kind of be yourself just makes them so much harder and just to be able to express yourself and to maintain a little more of a sense of dignity of like, this is who I am. This disease is not going to take that. I still have my voice. I still have my sense of humor. I still have my emotion that I can hopefully in the coming future express to people. It’s just so, so important.
paras.zh: 彼得罗夫斯基：我在这一领域的工作中学到的一件有趣的事情是，对于其中许多人来说，失去言语比失去行动能力更具破坏性，我不确定公众是否意识到这一点。你知道，你想想这些人经常不幸失去的东西：他们的行动能力、他们的独立性、他们的吞咽能力。但能够沟通将在某种程度上帮助他们解决所有这些问题。在没有声音或没有办法做自己的情况下经历所有这些变化只会让它们变得更加困难，而只是能够表达自己并保持更多的尊严感，这就是我。这种疾病不会接受这个。我仍然有我的声音。我仍然有我的幽默感。我仍然有我的情感，希望在不久的将来能够向人们表达。这就是如此、如此重要。

paras.en: Sanders: In 2022, two years after his ALS diagnosis, Jules’ voice started slipping away. MA had already thought about this inevitable moment, and she was dreading it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2022 年，即朱尔斯诊断出 ALS 两年后，朱尔斯的声音开始消失。妈妈已经想到了这个不可避免的时刻，她很害怕它。

paras.en: MA: Thinking back when I was at that time, and he was losing all of his physical abilities, you know, little by little, it’s like, you can no longer do this, and then that, and then that, and then that. And I always remember thinking, all of these things are breaking my heart, but when he loses his voice, I’m just going to shatter into a million pieces.
paras.zh: 马：回想我当时的情况，他的身体能力都在丧失，你知道，一点一点地，你不能再做这个，然后那个，然后那个，然后那个。我总是记得我在想，所有这些事情都让我心碎，但当他失去声音时，我就会碎成一百万块。

paras.en: Sanders: On the next episode of Talk To Me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在下一集《跟我说话》中。

paras.en: MA: I still remember the first time, this was in 2022, the summer of 22, that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA：我还记得第一次，那是在 2022 年，也就是 22 号的夏天，我听到他声音中的第一个小裂痕，让我知道有些事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Sanders: What does it feel like to stare down a future without a voice, especially for Jules? On his long-running podcast with MA, they talk about their lives, their family, their life that they’re building. They also talk about his ALS.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在没有声音的情况下凝视未来是什么感觉，尤其是对朱尔斯来说？在他与 MA 的长期播客中，他们谈论他们的生活、他们的家庭、他们正在建设的生活。他们还谈论了他的 ALS。

paras.en: Jules: It’s strange with the podcast because you can hear my real voice slowly decay till we stop.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：播客很奇怪，因为你可以听到我真实的声音慢慢衰减，直到我们停止。

paras.en: MA: Yeah, it really is this archive of what he sounded like little by little as it changed. And it was, yeah, like very disarming to get to that moment. And then you begin to get used to it, and you sort of work around it and you appreciate that it’s still there. But that was, yeah, that was really, really difficult for me.
paras.zh: MA：是的，这确实是他听起来一点一点改变的档案。是的，那一刻让人非常放松。然后你开始习惯它，你可以解决它，你会感激它仍然存在。但这对我来说真的非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: How much of Jules was his voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的声音有多少是朱尔斯的？

paras.en: Jules: For me, it felt like I was fading away. Like when Marty McFly was seeing his family fade away in the picture he had in “Back to the Future.”
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：对我来说，感觉就像我正在消失。就像马蒂·麦克弗莱在《回到未来》的照片中看到他的家人逐渐消失一样。

paras.en: Sanders: This is The Deep End, Season 2, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you liked this podcast, tell your friends. If you really like this podcast, leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts at sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：《这里是深渊》第二季，《跟我说话》。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友。如果您真的喜欢这个播客，请给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。通过 sciencenews.org 的播客向我们发送您的问题和评论。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor-in-chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特 (Nancy Shute) 是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.

articles.title: The world’s loudest bird could drown out a rock concert
articles.author: Elie Dolgin

paras.en: The bare-throated bellbird is loud. Very, very loud.
paras.zh: 裸喉钟鸟的声音很大。非常非常大声。

paras.en: The explosive, metallic mating call of the snow-white male — a stout bird with a broad bill and distinctive blue-green throat patch — can top 130 decibels, louder than a jackhammer or a front-row seat at a Counting Crows concert.
paras.zh: 雪白的雄鸟——一种粗壮的鸟，有着宽阔的喙和独特的蓝绿色喉咙斑——发出爆炸性的、金属般的求偶叫声，声音可达130分贝，比手提钻或数乌鸦音乐会前排座位的声音还要大。

paras.en: That makes this South American forest dweller a contender for the title of world’s loudest bird. And now researchers think they know how it and other avian loudmouths produce such eardrum-rattling vocalizations.
paras.zh: 这使得这种南美森林居民成为世界上声音最大的鸟类称号的有力竞争者。现在研究人员认为他们知道它和其他鸟类大嘴鸟是如何发出这种震耳欲聋的声音的。

paras.en: Bigger bodies and, especially, wider beaks help these feathered screamers belt it out, behavioral ecologists João Menezes and Jeff Podos of the University of Massachusetts Amherst report September 29 in Evolution.
paras.zh: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的行为生态学家 João Menezes 和 Jeff Podos 于 9 月 29 日在《进化论》杂志上报道称，更大的身体，尤其是更宽的喙有助于这些长有羽毛的尖叫鸟将其表达出来。

paras.en: But what pushed some birds to evolve such volume in the first place remains a mystery. The researchers looked at mating behavior, habitat density and flight ability, but found no explanation that consistently held across species. “We weren’t able to find an overarching pattern that applies to birds in general,” Menezes says.
paras.zh: 但最初是什么促使一些鸟类进化出如此大的体积仍然是一个谜。研究人员观察了交配行为、栖息地密度和飞行能力，但没有发现在不同物种之间一致成立的解释。 “我们无法找到适用于一般鸟类的总体模式，”梅内塞斯说。

paras.en: The quest to understand these sonic extremes dates back to 2019. That is when Podos and a colleague crowned the white bellbird (Procnias albus), an Amazonian cousin of the bare-throated bellbird (P. nudicollis), as a record-setting vocal powerhouse. Its 125-decibel calls were the loudest bird calls ever measured at the time.
paras.zh: 对这些声音极端现象的探索可以追溯到 2019 年。当时，波多斯和一位同事将白钟鸟 (Procnias albus)（裸喉钟鸟 (P. nudicollis) 的亚马逊近亲）评为创纪录的声音强者。它的叫声高达 125 分贝，是当时测量到的最响亮的鸟叫声。

paras.en: Beyond the attention-grabbing number, the finding raised a broader question: What makes some birds so extraordinarily loud?
paras.zh: 除了引人注目的数字之外，这一发现还提出了一个更广泛的问题：是什么让一些鸟类的声音如此之大？

paras.en: The honk of a Canada goose, for example, can reach chainsaw volume (100 decibels), while the chatter of a starling rarely rises above a dishwasher-level hum (70 decibels) — and ornithologists have surprisingly little understanding of why. Although scientists have spent decades cataloging the timing and frequency of birdsong, hoping to decode what birds are saying, the sheer loudness of bird voices has gone largely unexplored.
paras.zh: 例如，加拿大鹅的叫声可以达到电锯音量（100 分贝），而椋鸟的叫声很少会超过洗碗机级别的嗡嗡声（70 分贝）——令人惊讶的是，鸟类学家对其中的原因知之甚少。尽管科学家们花了几十年的时间对鸟鸣的时间和频率进行分类，希望能够解码鸟类所说的内容，但鸟类声音的响度在很大程度上还没有被探索过。

paras.en: To get a read on the racket, Podos lugged a high-grade sound meter, the kind used to monitor noise levels in industrial workplaces, and a laser rangefinder into the woods, swamps and open fields around his home in western Massachusetts. He measured the calls of whatever birds he could find — warblers, sparrows, robins and more.
paras.zh: 为了了解球拍情况，波多斯将一台高级声级计（用于监测工业工作场所噪音水平的那种）和一台激光测距仪拖进了他位于马萨诸塞州西部的家周围的树林、沼泽和开阔的田野。他测量了他能找到的所有鸟类的叫声——莺、麻雀、知更鸟等等。

paras.en: After logging a few dozen species, he enlisted Menezes, a then-grad student who at the time had recently joined his lab, to help turn the collection into a broader evolutionary analysis. Menezes measured bird vocalizations across his home country of Brazil, from the Atlantic Forest near São Paulo to the mountains surrounding Rio de Janeiro and beyond. He captured everything from the soft chirps of the dusky-throated hermit hummingbird to the piercing yelps of the red-legged seriema, a shaggy type of grassland bird.
paras.zh: 在记录了几十个物种后，他聘请了当时刚加入他实验室的研究生梅内塞斯来帮助将这些收集品转化为更广泛的进化分析。梅内塞斯测量了他的祖国巴西各地的鸟类发声，从圣保罗附近的大西洋森林到里约热内卢周围的山脉及更远的地方。他捕捉到了一切，从暗喉隐士蜂鸟的柔和鸣叫到红腿鸫（一种毛茸茸的草原鸟类）的刺耳叫声。

paras.en: All told, he and Podos compiled vocal volume data on 123 species, creating what they say is the largest such dataset to date.
paras.zh: 总而言之，他和 Podos 收集了 123 个物种的发声量数据，创建了他们所说的迄今为止最大的此类数据集。

paras.en: The heftier the bird, the louder its call tended to be, and the same went for birds with broader beaks — a connection between anatomy and acoustic performance that biophysicist Gabriel Mindlin from the University of Buenos Aires in Argentina finds “sensible and plausible.”
paras.zh: 鸟越重，它的叫声往往越大，对于喙部较宽的鸟来说也是如此——阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯大学的生物物理学家加布里埃尔·明德林认为，解剖学和声学性能之间的联系“合理且合理”。

paras.en: “Larger birds have the potential to generate greater respiratory pressures and flows, while morphological features such as beak opening can affect how efficiently acoustic energy radiates,” says Mindlin, who studies birdsong but was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: “较大的鸟类有可能产生更大的呼吸压力和流量，而喙张开等形态特征会影响声能的辐射效率，”研究鸟鸣但未参与这项工作的明德林说。

paras.en: Why evolution cranked up the volume on these avian megaphones, though, is a puzzle that remains, for now, unhatched.
paras.zh: 然而，为什么进化会提高这些鸟类扩音器的音量，目前仍然是一个尚未解开的谜团。

articles.title: ‘A Mother’s Brain’ explores the neuroscience of motherhood
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: When it comes to new motherhood, the baby typically takes center stage, garnering most of people’s attention. But in a refreshing twist, neuroscientist Susana Carmona shifts the spotlight to the mom. In the opening pages of A Mother’s Brain, Carmona cheerfully tells us, “here, we’ll hardly discuss babies at all.” Mothers are her protagonists.
paras.zh: 当谈到新妈妈时，婴儿通常占据中心舞台，吸引大多数人的注意力。但令人耳目一新的是，神经科学家苏珊娜·卡莫纳将焦点转移到了母亲身上。在《母亲的大脑》的开头几页中，卡莫纳愉快地告诉我们，“在这里，我们几乎不会讨论婴儿。”母亲是她的主角。

paras.en: What follows is a captivating, passionate and well-grounded journey through the fascinating process of “matrescence.” A word coined to echo “adolescence,” another time of seismic changes, matrescence includes the intense reorganization a woman’s brain undergoes as she becomes a mom. So far, early studies have revealed a sculpting of brain circuits (and Carmona is quick to point out that less can be more), heightened social instincts and perhaps even a boost of resilience during old age.
paras.zh: 接下来是一段引人入胜、充满激情且基础扎实的旅程，穿越令人着迷的“成熟期”过程。这个词是为了呼应“青春期”，即另一个发生巨大变化的时期，女性期包括女性在成为母亲后大脑所经历的剧烈重组。到目前为止，早期研究已经揭示了大脑回路的塑造（卡莫纳很快指出，少即是多）、社交本能的增强，甚至可能会增强老年时的适应力。

paras.en: This mom found the book to be a treasure trove of motherly delights. Scientific concepts are woven with social and cultural strands, from the poignant to the weird to the profound. Certain passages in the book allowed me the pleasure of relistening to the song “The Mother” by Brandi Carlile, in which she sings, “Welcome to the end of being alone inside your mind.” A Mother’s Brain also kindly pointed me to the viral video, “Mother Rat Saves Baby from Snake.”
paras.zh: 这位妈妈发现这本书是母爱的宝库。科学概念与社会和文化脉络交织在一起，从深刻到怪异到深刻。书中的某些段落让我有幸重听布兰迪·卡莱尔的歌曲《母亲》，她在歌中唱道：“欢迎来到你内心孤独的终结。” 《妈妈的大脑》还好心地向我推荐了一段火爆的视频：“鼠妈妈从蛇手中拯救了婴儿。”

paras.en: As one of the foremost scientists studying matrescence, Carmona is an authoritative guide through the latest research, of which there is a dismayingly small amount. Still, the book covers scientific ground including hormones, evolution and brain networks. History, social constructs and the pressures of modern life come into the story, too.
paras.zh: 作为研究基质形成的最重要的科学家之一，卡莫纳是最新研究的权威指南，但这些研究的数量少得令人沮丧。尽管如此，这本书涵盖了科学领域，包括激素、进化和大脑网络。历史、社会结构和现代生活的压力也出现在故事​​中。

paras.en: If you prefer a light read, Carmona will occasionally warn you when a section is scientifically dense. Then she will invite you along anyway. “But if you do like hormones — well, we’re going to have fun,” Carmona writes at the beginning of a chapter. And it was fun. I was shocked to learn, for instance, just how massive the hormonal upheaval during pregnancy is. The amount of estrogen that floods a woman’s body, including her brain, during the 40 weeks of pregnancy is more than that of the amount that would otherwise accumulate over her entire fertile life, which lasts 35 years on average.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢轻松阅读，卡莫纳偶尔会在某个部分的科学密度很高时向您发出警告。然后她无论如何都会邀请你一起去。 “但如果你确实喜欢荷尔蒙——好吧，我们会玩得很开心，”卡莫纳在章节开头写道。这很有趣。例如，当我得知怀孕期间荷尔蒙的波动有多大时，我感到震惊。在怀孕 40 周期间，女性体内（包括大脑）所分泌的雌激素数量，超过了她整个生育期（平均持续 35 年）所积累的雌激素量。

paras.en: Along the way, Carmona thoughtfully addresses scientific puzzlers such as this: Mothers often report feeling less mentally sharp, yet laboratory studies show almost no neurological decline. Attributed to “mommy brain” or “momnesia,” mental slips might be due to a lack of sleep, or a shifting of attention, or even just an expectation.
paras.zh: 在此过程中，卡莫纳深思熟虑地解决了诸如此类的科学难题：母亲们经常报告感觉精神不那么敏锐，但实验室研究显示几乎没有神经功能下降。被认为是“妈妈脑”或“记忆症”的精神失误可能是由于睡眠不足、注意力转移、甚至只是一种期望造成的。

paras.en: This pervasive, negative stereotype of “mommy brain” can then build on itself, getting stronger as women buy into the incorrect idea that motherhood leaves them dumber. If a woman expects her memory to get worse, she’ll see signs of it in even normal mistakes. “I have watched brilliant women grow so insecure about their intelligence on becoming mothers that they abandon the projects that were once vital to them,” Carmona writes. Assumptions about their diminished brainpower can lead women to pull back from valuable parts of their lives. “It matters — a lot — how we talk to ourselves about these things.”
paras.zh: 这种普遍存在的、消极的“妈妈脑”刻板印象会不断增强，随着女性接受“母性会让她们变得更笨”的错误观念，这种刻板印象会变得更加强烈。如果一个女人预计自己的记忆力会变差，那么即使是正常的错误，她也会看到这种迹象。卡莫纳写道：“我看到才华横溢的女性在成为母亲后对自己的智力变得如此不自信，以至于放弃了曾经对她们至关重要的项目。”对女性脑力下降的假设可能会导致女性放弃生活中有价值的部分。 “我们如何与自己谈论这些事情很重要。”

paras.en: As a mother herself, Carmona brings her experiences into the narrative. It couldn’t be any other way. “Motherhood is lived,” she writes. “It happens in your gut, your identity, your core.”
paras.zh: 作为一名母亲，卡莫纳将她的经历融入到叙述中。不可能有其他方式。 “母性是活生生的，”她写道。 “它发生在你的直觉、你的身份、你的核心。”

paras.en: At its heart, this book is a love letter to moms, who have been invisible to the scientific gaze for too long. It’s time to write a new tale of matrescence, Carmona argues. “A story that recognizes mothers as the essence of the human species, the carriers of knowledge about how we create bonds — and, through them, society and culture.”
paras.zh: 从本质上讲，这本书是一封写给妈妈们的情书，她们已经在科学的视线中消失太久了。卡莫纳认为，是时候写一个新的女性成长故事了。 “这个故事承认母亲是人类的本质，是我们如何建立联系的知识载体，并通过母亲建立社会和文化。”

paras.en: By putting the intense and wild changes of motherhood into words, Carmona offers us a powerful and necessary story.
paras.zh: 通过用语言表达母性的强烈而疯狂的变化，卡莫纳为我们提供了一个有力而必要的故事。
