articles.title: The 2029 tipping point: Western populations are about to start shrinking, piling pressure on public finances

paras.en: As Western populations age, fewer workers and higher costs will strain public finances, credit rating agency Moody's has warned.
paras.zh: 信用评级机构穆迪警告称，随着西方人口老龄化，劳动力减少和成本上升将给公共财政带来压力。

paras.en: Europe is at the sharp end of the demographic shift. The European Union's population is projected to peak as soon as 2029, "after which a sustained long-term decline will begin," according to the European Commission.
paras.zh: 欧洲正处于人口结构转变的最高峰。欧盟委员会表示，预计欧盟人口最早将于 2029 年达到峰值，“此后将开始持续长期下降”。

paras.en: The U.S. Census Bureau does not expect the American population to peak until 2080 under its main projection, or until 2043 under its low-immigration scenario. Excluding immigration impact, the population decline has already started.
paras.zh: 美国人口普查局预计，根据其主要预测，美国人口要到 2080 年才会达到峰值；根据其低移民情景，美国人口要到 2043 年才会达到峰值。排除移民影响，人口下降已经开始。

paras.en: But Moody's says the fiscal pressures from aging emerge long before populations actually start shrinking.
paras.zh: 但穆迪表示，老龄化带来的财政压力早在人口实际开始萎缩之前就已经出现。

paras.en: Today, G7 economies have about three working-age people for every person over 65. That ratio is expected to fall to around two by 2050, putting further pressure on growth and public finances, including healthcare systems, according to Moody's.
paras.zh: 如今，七国集团经济体中每 65 岁以上的人就有 3 名适龄劳动人口。穆迪表示，到 2050 年，这一比例预计将降至 2 左右，从而给经济增长和包括医疗保健系统在内的公共财政带来进一步压力。

paras.en: Aging populations affect economies through slower economic growth, greater pressure on public finances from pension and care costs, changing consumer demand, and shifts in real interest rates and sovereign yields, Olivier Chemla, vice president of credit strategy and standards at Moody's, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday.
paras.zh: 穆迪信贷战略和标准副总裁奥利维尔·切姆拉 (Olivier Chemla) 周五在 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目中表示，人口老龄化通过经济增长放缓、养老金和护理成本对公共财政造成更大压力、消费者需求变化以及实际利率和主权收益率变化等因素对经济产生影响。

paras.en: In a report published last week, Moody's forecasts that the world's aging populations will have fundamental impacts on the global economy and lead to difficult policy decisions.
paras.zh: 穆迪在上周发布的一份报告中预测，世界人口老龄化将对全球经济产生根本性影响，并导致艰难的政策决策。

paras.en: While population growth has long been a tailwind for growth and creditworthiness, falling fertility rates and unprecedented speed of changing age structures are now changing that picture, Moody's writes.
paras.zh: 穆迪写道，虽然人口增长长期以来一直是经济增长和信用度的推动力，但生育率下降和年龄结构前所未有的变化速度现在正在改变这种情况。

paras.en: "Fewer workers will limit productive capacity, while fewer households and consumers will weaken demand. As a result, countries will have to rely more on productivity to sustain growth," the report states.
paras.zh: 报告指出：“工人减少将限制生产能力，而家庭和消费者减少将削弱需求。因此，各国将不得不更多地依赖生产力来维持增长。”

paras.en: AI and increased productivity can only partially offset the long-term challenge of an aging workforce, Chemla said.
paras.zh: Chemla 表示，人工智能和生产力的提高只能部分抵消劳动力老龄化带来的长期挑战。

paras.en: "This is a partial mitigant because you can certainly replace and enhance the supply side of the economy in factories and in services, but at the same time, robots do not consume – at least not yet – and so on the demand side, you will still be having that gap, which will slow growth," he added.
paras.zh: 他补充说：“这是一种部分缓解措施，因为你当然可以取代和增强工厂和服务业的经济供给面，但与此同时，机器人不会消费——至少现在还没有——因此在需求方面，你仍然会存在这种差距，这将减缓增长。”

paras.en: And it's not only Europe and the U.S., but emerging economies are aging rapidly, too. China's share of people aged 65 and over has doubled from 7% to 14% over the past two decades, with Brazil, Thailand and Turkiye on similar trajectories.
paras.zh: 不仅欧洲和美国，新兴经济体也在迅速老龄化。过去20年，中国65岁及以上人口的比例翻了一番，从7%增至14%，巴西、泰国和土耳其也处于类似的轨迹。

paras.en: These countries will face the costs of aging at much lower income levels than the advanced economies that aged before them, the report says, noting that in Europe, the same shift took several decades.
paras.zh: 报告称，这些国家将面临比先于老龄化的发达经济体低得多的收入水平的老龄化成本，并指出在欧洲，同样的转变花费了几十年的时间。

articles.title: Russia hospitalizes almost 200 people after researcher's death from plague: Reports

paras.en: Nearly 200 people have been placed under medical observation in Russia's Irkutsk region in eastern Siberia over suspected exposure to plague, according to local media reports.
paras.zh: 据当地媒体报道，俄罗斯东西伯利亚伊尔库茨克地区已有近200人因疑似感染鼠疫而接受医学观察。

paras.en: The report said 189 people were being monitored following the illness of an employee at an anti-plague research institute in Irkutsk. Alexei Tsydenov, head of the nearby Republic of Buryatia, said the woman had died from an unspecified form of plague.
paras.zh: 报告称，伊尔库茨克一家抗鼠疫研究所一名员工患病后，189 人正在接受监测。附近的布里亚特共和国总统阿列克谢·齐德诺夫 (Alexei Tsydenov) 表示，这名妇女死于一种不明形式的鼠疫。

paras.en: Russia's public health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said Sunday that the employee had been diagnosed with "pneumonia of unknown etiology" and that the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region and the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov remained stable.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯公共卫生监管机构Rospotrebnadzor周日表示，该员工被诊断出患有“不明原因肺炎”，伊尔库茨克地区以及伊尔库茨克市和谢列霍夫市的卫生和流行病学状况保持稳定。

paras.en: The agency said expanded testing had not detected microorganisms linked to the employee's work.
paras.zh: 该机构表示，扩大测试并未检测到与该员工工作相关的微生物。

paras.en: The update follows local media reports on Friday that a 27-year-old employee at an anti-plague institute had fallen ill with suspected pneumonic plague after returning from a work trip to Buryatia, where an outbreak had been reported near the border with Mongolia, citing Russian Telegram channel Mash.
paras.zh: 当地媒体周五援引俄罗斯 Telegram 频道 Mash 报道称，一家抗鼠疫研究所的一名 27 岁员工从布里亚特出差回来后疑似患上肺鼠疫。布里亚特在与蒙古边境附近爆发了疫情。

paras.en: The White House is monitoring reports of the suspected case and related quarantines in Russia, Axios reported Sunday, citing a Trump administration official. The official said the administration was "aware, monitoring the outbreak, and assessing options," the report said.
paras.zh: Axios 周日援引特朗普政府官员的话说，白宫正在监视俄罗斯疑似病例和相关隔离的报告。报告称，这位官员表示，政府“已经意识到这一点，正在监测疫情并评估选择”。

paras.en: The Russian and Moscow ministries of health, the World Health Organization and the U.S. State Department did not immediately respond to CNBC's requests for comment.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯和莫斯科卫生部、世界卫生组织和美国国务院没有立即回应 CNBC 的置评请求。

articles.title: Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes: Live updates

paras.en: Stock futures were little changed early Monday as elevated Treasury yields dented investor sentiment with focus on minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting for clues about the central bank's next interest rate move.
paras.zh: 周一早盘股指期货几乎没有变化，因为美国国债收益率的上升削弱了投资者的情绪，投资者关注的是美联储最新会议纪要，以寻找有关央行下一步利率变动的线索。

paras.en: Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 51 points, or 0.1%, and S&P 500 futures was flat, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.2%
paras.zh: 道琼斯工业平均指数期货下跌 51 点，即 0.1%，标准普尔 500 指数期货持平，纳斯达克 100 指数期货上涨 0.2%

paras.en: In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 added 2.2%, while the broader Topix rose 0.79%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.12% higher. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was flat. Markets in mainland China and South Korea were closed for holidays.
paras.zh: 在亚洲，日本日经 225 指数上涨 2.2%，而更广泛的东证指数上涨 0.79%。澳大利亚基准 S&P/ASX 200 指数上涨 0.12%。香港恒生指数持平。中国大陆和韩国市场因假期休市。

paras.en: On Friday, U.S. stocks rose to close out the week, with the blue-chip Dow adding 250 points, or 0.5%, to close at 51,176.46, while the broad market S&P 500 climbed 0.7% to 7,722.72. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rallied 1.2% to 27,190.86, after hitting an all-time high earlier in the session.
paras.zh: 周五，美国股市上涨，收盘一周，蓝筹道指上涨 250 点，或 0.5%，收于 51,176.46 点，而大盘标准普尔 500 指数上涨 0.7%，至 7,722.72 点。以科技股为主的纳斯达克综合指数在盘中早些时候触及历史新高后，上涨 1.2% 至 27,190.86 点。

paras.en: Stocks are coming off a week defined by surging Treasury yields and a surprisingly lackluster jobs report that helped ease concerns about another Fed rate hike this month. The data provided some relief after a week of pressure from rising bond yields.
paras.zh: 美国国债收益率飙升和就业报告出人意料地低迷，这有助于缓解人们对美联储本月再次加息的担忧，这使得股市下跌。在经历了一周债券收益率上升的压力之后，该数据缓解了一些压力。

paras.en: Still, Treasury yields remain a key focus for investors, with the 10-year yield climbing to its highest level in more than two decades and raising concerns that higher borrowing costs could weigh on stocks even if the Fed holds rates steady in the near term.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，美国国债收益率仍然是投资者关注的焦点，10年期国债收益率攀升至二十多年来的最高水平，并引发人们的担忧，即即使美联储在短期内维持利率稳定，借贷成本上升也可能会给股​​市带来压力。

paras.en: Tech stocks led Friday's advance, with Nvidia hitting an all-time high intraday and the Nasdaq reaching a record. Investors will be watching whether that momentum carries into the new week.
paras.zh: 科技股周五领涨，英伟达盘中创历史新高，纳斯达克指数创历史新高。投资者将关注这种势头是否会延续到新的一周。

paras.en: With a light economic calendar ahead, investors will be watching geopolitical and market developments before earnings season gets underway.
paras.zh: 由于经济日历清淡，投资者将在财报季节开始之前关注地缘政治和市场发展。

paras.en: "The light data calendar means that the investors will be responding to the ebb and flow of geopolitical and market specific developments matched against the latest batch of reasonably supportive economic reports, all ahead of the unofficial start of the reporting season with JP Morgan's results on October 13," said Gary Schlossberg, global strategist for Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
paras.zh: 富国银行投资研究所全球策略师加里·施洛斯伯格表示：“数据较少意味着投资者将对地缘政治和市场特定发展的潮起潮落做出反应，并与最新一批相当支持性的经济报告相匹配，所有这些都在 10 月 13 日摩根大通财报季非正式开始之前进行。”

paras.en: On Monday, investors will be watching the Institute for Supply Management's services activity report. Also on the calendar are minutes from the Fed's September meeting on Wednesday and the University of Michigan's preliminary October consumer sentiment reading, due Friday.
paras.zh: 周一，投资者将关注供应管理协会的服务活动报告。日历上还包括周三美联储 9 月份会议纪要以及周五公布的密歇根大学 10 月份消费者信心指数初步数据。

paras.en: Still on deck this week for the current earnings season are Constellation Brands, Levi Strauss, PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines and others.
paras.zh: 本周，星座品牌、李维斯、百事可乐、达美航空等公司仍在准备迎接当前的财报季。

articles.title: Scientists are decoding elephant rumble calls, including ‘greetings’ and ‘coos’

paras.en: In February 2020 behavioral ecologist Mickey Pardo witnessed the aftermath of an elephant birth. In Kenya’s Samburu National Reserve, he watched as a female African elephant named Matisse called to her newborn with repeated “rumbles”—a kind of deep vocalization he describes as like “an idling truck engine.” Pardo watched as another adult elephant, likely Matisse’s sister, rumbled from a distance before the family came together, uniting with another series of rumbles, as if saying hello.
paras.zh: 2020 年 2 月，行为生态学家米基·帕尔多 (Mickey Pardo) 目睹了大象出生的后果。在肯尼亚的桑布鲁国家保护区，他看到一头名叫马蒂斯的雌性非洲象用重复的“隆隆声”呼唤她的新生儿——他将这种低沉的声音描述为“空转的卡车引擎”。帕尔多看着另一头成年大象，可能是马蒂斯的妹妹，在一家人聚集在一起之前从远处发出隆隆声，与另一系列隆隆声结合在一起，好像在打招呼。

paras.en: “It was just really ... fascinating to see this whole sequence,” recalls Pardo, a senior scientist at the research organization ElephantVoices. What these calls might mean, exactly, has long been a mystery. But a new study published on Thursday in Scientific Reports helps to shed some light.
paras.zh: “看到这整个序列真是……令人着迷，”研究组织 ElephantVoices 的高级科学家帕尔多回忆道。这些电话到底意味着什么，长期以来一直是个谜。但周四发表在《科学报告》上的一项新研究有助于揭示一些真相。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In the study, Pardo and a team of scientists used machine learning to analyze hundreds of rumble recordings from a separate population of African elephants in Amboseli National Park, also in Kenya.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，帕尔多和一组科学家利用机器学习分析了来自同样位于肯尼亚安博塞利国家公园的不同非洲象种群的数百个隆隆声录音。

paras.en: The analysis homes in on several kinds of elephant rumbles: “coo” rumbles to calves, “contact” rumbles made from a distance, “let’s-go” rumbles before group movements, “cadenced” rumbles during rest or meals and two different “greeting” rumbles.
paras.zh: 分析的重点是大象的几种隆隆声：对小牛的“咕咕”隆隆声、从远处发出的“接触”隆隆声、群体运动前的“走吧”隆隆声、休息或进餐时的“有节奏”隆隆声以及两种不同的“问候”隆隆声。

paras.en: In many cases, the recordings captured overlapping calls, a jumble of rumbles the researchers refer to as “choruses.” To be clear, these calls are not at all like elephants’ iconic trumpet sound. They are low and almost like a growl or thunder.
paras.zh: 在许多情况下，录音捕获了重叠的呼叫，研究人员将这些混乱的隆隆声称为“合唱”。需要明确的是，这些叫声根本不像大象标志性的喇叭声。它们声音很低，几乎像咆哮或雷声。

paras.en: The researchers used the algorithm to predict the elephants’ behavior based on each recording. It wasn’t entirely accurate, but it did predict behaviors better than chance—suggesting that elephant vocalizations during similar situations may have similar acoustic properties.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用该算法根据每个记录来预测大象的行为。它并不完全准确，但它确实比偶然更好地预测了行为——这表明大象在相似情况下的发声可能具有相似的声学特性。

paras.en: “It is pretty exciting that we’re able to train a model to look at an entire chorus and have some interpretation of exactly what’s going on,” says Sara Keen, a study co-author and a senior research scientist at the nonprofit Earth Species Project.
paras.zh: “非常令人兴奋的是，我们能够训练一个模型来观察整个合唱团，并对正在发生的事情做出一些解释，”非营利性地球物种项目的研究合著者和高级研究科学家萨拉·基恩（Sara Keen）说。

paras.en: In some cases, different rumbles became progressively similar, a pattern the researchers describe as “vocal convergence.” Scientists have observed this phenomenon in other chatty animals, including parrots and dolphins. Humans, too, are known to mirror one another’s language patterns.
paras.zh: 在某些情况下，不同的隆隆声变得越来越相似，研究人员将这种模式描述为“声音趋同”。科学家们在其他爱说话的动物身上观察到了这种现象，包括鹦鹉和海豚。众所周知，人类也会模仿彼此的语言模式。

paras.en: Interestingly, converging appeared “only in the situations where they [the elephants] seem to be coordinating group behavior action,” Keen says. It’s possible that this convergence could indicate agreement, but that theory needs further testing to confirm, she adds.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，“只有在它们（大象）似乎正在协调群体行为行动的情况下”才会出现聚合，基恩说。她补充说，这种趋同可能表明达成了一致，但该理论需要进一步测试来证实。

paras.en: “This study emphasizes how vital it is to pair new computational analyses with real behavioral observations in the wild,” says Arik Kershenbaum, a zoologist at the University of Cambridge, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: “这项研究强调了将新的计算分析与野外真实行为观察结合起来的重要性，”剑桥大学动物学家阿里克·克申鲍姆（Arik Kershenbaum）说，他没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: Keen hopes scientists may be able to use similar methods to analyze other animal calls, too, such as for orcas and crows. Many other species are known to perform a kind of “chorusing,” she says, which may make good candidates for future research.
paras.zh: 基恩希望科学家们也能够使用类似的方法来分析其他动物的叫声，例如虎鲸和乌鸦的叫声。她说，许多其他物种都知道会进行某种“合唱”，这可能是未来研究的良好候选者。

paras.en: “Animals communicate to influence each other’s behavior, and so you can’t just study the sounds in isolation,” Kershenbaum explains. “But when you combine a rich behavioral dataset with powerful machine learning algorithms, that’s when we can start to get answers to questions like ‘What are the animals saying?’”
paras.zh: “动物通过交流来影响彼此的行为，因此你不能仅仅孤立地研究声音，”克申鲍姆解释道。 “但是，当你将丰富的行为数据集与强大的机器学习算法结合起来时，我们就可以开始获得诸如‘动物在说什么？’之类的问题的答案。”

articles.title: Google tests its plan for AI data centers in space with Project Suncatcher

paras.en: When Elon Musk took SpaceX public in June, a big part of its value proposition came from promises of data centers in space. Skeptics were quick to list all of the hurdles. This afternoon Google’s Project Suncatcher is scheduled to launch hardware in pursuit of the same idea: it will send artificial intelligence processors into orbit onboard—of all things—a SpaceX rocket.
paras.zh: 当埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 6 月将 SpaceX 上市时，其价值主张的很大一部分来自于太空数据中心的承诺。怀疑论者很快列出了所有障碍。今天下午，谷歌的 Suncatcher 项目计划发射硬件，以实现同样的想法：它将把人工智能处理器搭载在 SpaceX 火箭上送入轨道。

paras.en: That doesn’t mean Musk’s pitch will become reality anytime soon. If anything, the gulf between Suncatcher and a working data center in orbit suggests how far off that future still is. But as AI’s appetite for electricity tests the patience of communities being asked to feed it, some of the richest tech companies are racing to source their energy needs from space instead.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着马斯克的主张很快就会成为现实。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是“捕日者”号和在轨运行的数据中心之间的鸿沟表明，这个未来还很遥远。但随着人工智能对电力的需求考验着被要求提供电力的社区的耐心，一些最富有的科技公司正在竞相从太空获取能源需求。

paras.en: The test satellite will carry just four processors, which will be used to run Google’s Gemini AI models for 15 minutes at a stretch before they need to shut down and cool off. The ultimate goal is to establish a full-fledged orbital data center, built from constellations of thousands of satellites that will share the work of running AI models and beam their responses back to Earth.
paras.zh: 该测试卫星将仅搭载四个处理器，用于连续运行谷歌的 Gemini AI 模型 15 分钟，然后它们需要关闭并冷却。最终目标是建立一个成熟的轨道数据中心，由数千颗卫星组成的星座组成，这些卫星将共享运行人工智能模型的工作并将其响应传回地球。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The whole effort has less to do with what could be accomplished out in space than with what’s getting harder to achieve down here on Earth. Data centers are projected to use around 3 percent of the world’s electricity by 2030, roughly double their share today, according to an International Energy Agency report. In orbit, sunlight is abundant and free, and Google says a solar panel there generates up to eight times as much power as it would on the ground. “We have direct access to a wonderful renewable source of energy,” says Alexander Wyglinski, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Worcester Polytechnic Institute.
paras.zh: 整个努力与在太空中可以完成的事情无关，而与在地球上越来越难以实现的事情有关。根据国际能源署的一份报告，预计到 2030 年，数据中心将使用全球约 3% 的电力，大约是目前份额的两倍。在轨道上，阳光充足且免费，谷歌表示，那里的太阳能电池板产生的电力最多是地面上的八倍。 “我们可以直接获得美妙的可再生能源，”伍斯特理工学院电气和计算机工程教授亚历山大·威格林斯基 (Alexander Wyglinski) 说。

paras.en: There’s a political incentive to look beyond U.S. soil, too. As the data-center buildout grows more divisive, blasting that infrastructure into space and away from people’s backyards holds obvious appeal.
paras.zh: 放眼美国本土之外也有政治动机。随着数据中心建设的分歧越来越大，将基础设施投入太空并远离人们的后院显然具有吸引力。

paras.en: But scale is the main question, Google readily admits. The biggest AI data centers that are being built now pack in hundreds of thousands of chips and draw up to a gigawatt of power, several thousand times the output of the International Space Station’s solar arrays. Even getting enough solar panels into orbit would be a massive undertaking at that scale. “It’s going from arrays that are several meters on a side to arrays that are a couple of kilometers on a side,” says Kerri Cahoy, a professor of astronautics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. “Launching enough mass to generate the power is huge.”
paras.zh: 但谷歌欣然承认，规模是主要问题。目前正在建设的最大的人工智能数据中心配备了数十万个芯片，消耗的电力达到千兆瓦，是国际空间站太阳能电池阵列输出的数千倍。在这种规模下，即使将足够的太阳能电池板送入轨道也是一项艰巨的任务。麻省理工学院宇航学教授 Kerri Cahoy 表示：“它正在从边长几米的阵列变成边长几公里的阵列。” “发射足够的质量来产生能量是巨大的。”

paras.en: The problems don’t end once everything is up there, either. Though space is cold, its vacuum is a lousy place to dissipate heat, which is why Suncatcher’s chips must clock out to cool down and why the satellites require specialized radiators. The whole satellite network needs to be resilient to space debris. And the cosmic radiation that Earth’s atmosphere filters out can scramble calculations, forcing systems to catch and correct errors on the fly. “When we talk about satellite platforms, and you put a computer into them, you don’t put [in] a computer like the one you have on your desk,” Wyglinski says.
paras.zh: 一旦一切就绪，问题也不会结束。尽管太空很冷，但其真空却是一个散热不良的地方，这就是为什么“捕日者”号的芯片必须计时以冷却的原因，也是卫星需要专门散热器的原因。整个卫星网络需要能够抵御空间碎片。地球大气层过滤掉的宇宙辐射会扰乱计算，迫使系统即时捕捉和纠正错误。 “当我们谈论卫星平台时，你将一台计算机放入其中，但你所放入的计算机与你桌上的计算机不同，”维格林斯基说。

paras.en: For months before today’s launch, Google has been anticipating those problems on Earth, shaking spacecraft to simulate the launch and bombarding its chips with proton beams to test their response to radiation. “It's about seeing what works, identifying points of failure and applying those findings to future missions,” says Travis Beals, a senior director at Google, who leads Project Suncatcher.
paras.zh: 在今天发射之前的几个月里，谷歌一直在预测地球上的这些问题，摇动航天器来模拟发射，并用质子束轰击其芯片来测试它们对辐射的反应。 “关键是要看看什么是有效的，找出失败点，并将这些发现应用到未来的任务中，”领导 Suncatcher 项目的谷歌高级总监特拉维斯·比尔斯 (Travis Beals) 说。

paras.en: Even so, scaling up could force Google and SpaceX to confront some stubborn physics. Every chip and solar panel has to be hauled into orbit, and every answer those chips produce has to come back down.
paras.zh: 即便如此，扩大规模可能会迫使谷歌和 SpaceX 面对一些顽固的物理现象。每个芯片和太阳能电池板都必须被拖入轨道，并且这些芯片产生的每个答案都必须返回。

paras.en: Satellites can transmit data to Earth, but doing so at scale is expensive and difficult. “We don’t have the convenient, easy way to get that data back to the ground,” says Alan George, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Pittsburgh, who heads a National Science Foundation center focused on space computing. During the Cold War, the problem was bad enough that U.S. spy satellites parachuted exposed film back to Earth.
paras.zh: 卫星可以向地球传输数据，但大规模传输数据既昂贵又困难。 “我们没有方便、简单的方法将数据传回地面，”匹兹堡大学电气和计算机工程教授艾伦·乔治（Alan George）说，他是一个专注于空间计算的国家科学基金会中心的负责人。冷战期间，这个问题非常严重，以至于美国间谍卫星将曝光的胶片空投回地球。

paras.en: Computers on Earth relay information easily, and lasers have made it possible to do the same between spacecraft. But getting information between Earth and space is another story entirely, so it is best to process some of the information gathered on satellites before it is sent down to Earth. “I like to tell my students the best data compression is answers,” George says. While that logic could apply to AI responses, too, his work putting computers in space tells him that the resource constraints make it hard to match what “you would put down the street in a building.”
paras.zh: 地球上的计算机可以轻松地传递信息，激光使得航天器之间的信息传递成为可能。但在地球和太空之间获取信息完全是另一回事，因此最好在卫星上收集的一些信息发送到地球之前对其进行处理。 “我喜欢告诉我的学生最好的数据压缩就是答案，”乔治说。虽然这种逻辑也适用于人工智能响应，但他将计算机放入太空的工作告诉他，资源限制使其很难匹配“你将在建筑物中的街道上放置的东西”。

paras.en: Google’s engineers say they began from a similarly skeptical premise. “As a first step, we tried to find reasons that it was impossible,” Beals says, “but we gradually became convinced that it might actually work.”
paras.zh: 谷歌的工程师表示，他们也是从同样持怀疑态度的前提出发的。比尔斯说：“作为第一步，我们试图找出这是不可能的原因，但我们逐渐相信它可能确实有效。”

paras.en: And then there’s the question that may ultimately decide the whole thing: How will the limited bandwidth and energy savings make up the maintenance costs?
paras.zh: 还有一个问题可能最终决定整个事情：有限的带宽和节能将如何弥补维护成本？

paras.en: The cost of launching data center satellites and replacing them as they wear out, along with the bottleneck of getting data back down, may eat up whatever the free sunshine saves. The competitors in the first space race were nations jockeying for scientific dominance. Orbital data centers are mainly being pitched by corporations, which tend to prefer profitable ventures. So even if Project Suncatcher solves its technical challenges, those physical limitations could still kill the idea before Google gets anywhere close to a full-blown data center in space.
paras.zh: 发射数据中心卫星并在其磨损时更换它们的成本，以及恢复数据的瓶颈，可能会耗尽免费阳光节省下来的一切。第一次太空竞赛的竞争者是争夺科学主导地位的国家。轨道数据中心主要由企业推销，而企业往往更喜欢盈利的企业。因此，即使“Suncatcher”项目解决了其技术挑战，在谷歌接近建立一个成熟的太空数据中心之前，这些物理限制仍然可能会扼杀这个想法。

paras.en: More often than not, space throws up more challenges than early movers expect. “It’s usually the late entrants who finally figured out how to do it effectively,” Cahoy says. SpaceX itself didn’t reach orbit until half a century after Sputnik.
paras.zh: 通常，太空带来的挑战比先行者预期的要多。卡霍伊说：“通常是后来的进入者最终找到了如何有效地做到这一点。”直到人造卫星发射半个世纪后，SpaceX 才进入轨道。

paras.en: If she’s right, the company that eventually gets data centers in space to scale may not even have booked its ride to orbit yet.
paras.zh: 如果她是对的，那么最终在太空中扩大数据中心规模的公司可能还没有预订进入轨道的旅程。

articles.title: Scientists discover that Earth’s crust has repeatedly rolled over—and it’s still happening

paras.en: Several times since the age of dinosaurs, the solid part of our planet has rolled over, drowning some continents and lifting others out of the sea.
paras.zh: 自恐龙时代以来，我们星球的固体部分已经发生过好几次翻滚，淹没了一些大陆，将另一些大陆从海中升起。

paras.en: Our planet is slightly squished, with more mass at the equator. But the movement of Earth’s mantle and rocky crust can make some areas denser than others and throw off the planet’s balance. As a result, these solid outer layers can tilt and slide around the planet’s liquid inner core beneath as the planet works to redistribute its mass. This phenomenon is called true polar wander because it moves the planet’s actual rather than magnetic poles.
paras.zh: 我们的星球被轻微挤压，赤道处的质量更大。但地幔和岩壳的运动可能会使某些区域比其他区域密度更大，从而打破地球的平衡。因此，当行星努力重新分配其质量时，这些固体外层可以围绕行星下方的液体内核倾斜和滑动。这种现象被称为真正的极移，因为它移动的是地球的实际极点而不是磁极。

paras.en: Incredibly, a new Science study finds this massive upheaval has happened to our planet at least four times in the past 320 million years. And it’s still ongoing.
paras.zh: 令人难以置信的是，一项新的科学研究发现，在过去 3.2 亿年里，我们的星球至少发生了四次这种巨大的剧变。而且它仍在继续。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “Based on satellite measurements, we know that this is happening today, at about 10 centimeters a year, mainly because of melting ice caps,” says Mathew Domeier, a geoscientist at the University of Oslo and lead author of the study.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、奥斯陆大学地球科学家马修·多梅尔 (Mathew Domeier) 表示：“根据卫星测量，我们知道这种情况正在以每年约 10 厘米的速度发生，主要是因为冰盖融化。”

paras.en: What scientists didn’t know was whether true polar wander is a slow, steady process that’s always going on or happens in short, rapid bursts. The best evidence scientists had for the phenomenon was from magnetic signals recorded in ancient rocks, but those are sparse and inconclusive. So instead Domeier’s team looked at clues hidden in ancient floods.
paras.zh: 科学家们不知道的是，真正的极地漂移是否是一个缓慢、稳定的过程，总是持续进行，还是在短暂、快速的爆发中发生。科学家们对这种现象的最佳证据来自古代岩石中记录的磁信号，但这些证据很少且没有结论。因此，多梅尔的团队转而寻找古代洪水中隐藏的线索。

paras.en: Earth’s spin makes both the planet’s rock and water bulge at the equator. When the solid Earth tips out of alignment, it is driven through the watery bulge, and parts of the rock poke out of the water while others get drowned. It looks like sea-level change, but that’s not the case at all, Domeier says: The water stays put while the continents move. Two opposing quarters of the globe flood, while the other two dry out, forming a unique four-leaf-clover pattern.
paras.zh: 地球的自转使地球的岩石和水在赤道处隆起。当固体地球倾斜失准时，它会被推动穿过水状隆起部分，部分岩石从水中伸出，而另一些则被淹没。多梅尔说，这看起来像是海平面变化，但事实并非如此：当大陆移动时，水保​​持不变。地球上相对的两个区域被洪水淹没，而另外两个区域则干旱，形成了独特的四叶草图案。

paras.en: The team analyzed maps showing where continents lay underwater or dry at 10-million-year time points. The four-leaf-clover pattern appears around 200, 150 and 100 million years ago, and again between 30 and 20 million years ago. The findings, Domeier says, “took me quite by surprise.”
paras.zh: 研究小组分析了显示一千万年时间点上大陆处于水下或干燥位置的地图。四叶草图案出现于大约 200、150 和 1 亿年前，以及 30 至 2000 万年前。多梅尔说，这一发现“让我非常惊讶”。

paras.en: “The particularly elegant aspect of this study is the independent test it provides” for the existing magnetic data, says Giovanni Muttoni, a geologist at the University of Milan, who wasn’t involved in the new research. The strongest signal found, from 150 to 140 million years ago, he notes, matches a period for which magnetic data had already hinted at rapid wander.
paras.zh: 米兰大学的地质学家乔瓦尼·穆托尼（Giovanni Muttoni）没有参与这项新研究，他说：“这项研究特别优雅的方面是它为现有的磁力数据提供了独立测试。”他指出，在 150 至 1.4 亿年前发现的最强信号，与磁力数据已经暗示存在快速漂移的时期相符。

paras.en: “During true polar wander, continents can move rapidly across the climate belts even though their positions relative to one another change much less,” Muttoni says. This rapid movement could reshape ocean currents, upend ecosystems and perhaps even nudge Earth’s magnetic field.
paras.zh: “在真正的极地漂移过程中，大陆可以快速穿过气候带，尽管它们相对于彼此的位置变化要小得多，”穆托尼说。这种快速运动可能会重塑洋流、颠覆生态系统，甚至可能推动地球磁场。

paras.en: What exactly triggers rapid true polar wander events and how far the poles move during them remains unknown. “Trying to understand why these events happened at these times would be the next logical step,” Domeier says.
paras.zh: 到底是什么触发了快速的真正的极地漂移事件以及极地在极移过程中移动了多远仍然未知。 “尝试了解为什么这些事件在这些时间发生将是下一个合乎逻辑的步骤，”多梅尔说。

articles.title: Peru’s penguins are on the brink. A super El Niño could make it worse.
articles.author: Ana Elisa Sotelo

paras.en: The first time I was in Punta San Juan, the desert was flooded with birds. It was 2012, and I was making a short documentary film about the cormorants, pelicans and penguins that made this arid peninsula in southern Peru one of the largest gatherings of seabirds on Earth.
paras.zh: 我第一次来到蓬塔圣胡安时，沙漠里到处都是鸟类。那是 2012 年，我正在制作一部关于鸬鹚、鹈鹕和企鹅的纪录片短片，它们使秘鲁南部的这个干旱半岛成为地球上最大的海鸟聚集地之一。

paras.en: At the time, this 133-acre reserve — a patch of rock and sand jutting into the frigid waters of the Pacific Ocean — was home to more than a quarter million seabirds, including 300,000 Guanay cormorants (Leucocarbo bougainvilliorum) and some 3,000 Humboldt penguins (Spheniscus humboldti).
paras.zh: 当时，这个占地 133 英亩的保护区——一片伸入太平洋寒冷海水的岩石和沙子——是超过 25 万只海鸟的家园，其中包括 30 万只关奈鸬鹚 (Leucocarbo bougainvilliorum) 和约 3,000 只洪堡企鹅 (Spheniscus humboldti)。

paras.en: One of the few species of desert penguin, the Humboldt live along the arid coast of Peru and Chile, where they nest in burrows dug into guano deposits or small cliff caves. Punta San Juan was home to the largest colony in Peru.
paras.zh: 洪堡企鹅是为数不多的沙漠企鹅之一，生活在秘鲁和智利的干旱海岸，它们在鸟粪沉积物或小悬崖洞穴中挖的洞穴中筑巢。蓬塔圣胡安是秘鲁最大殖民地的所在地。

paras.en: By 2025, there were fewer than 500 penguins left. Avian flu had spread through the reserve in 2022 and 2023, crashing seabird populations and spreading to marine mammals such as sea lions and seals. El Niño struck next. The climate pattern is characterized by months of warmer than usual sea surface temperatures in the eastern equatorial Pacific. Those warm waters pushed anchovy — the penguins’ main food source — deeper and farther out to sea. Industrial fishing operations put even more pressure on the surviving animals.
paras.zh: 到 2025 年，企鹅数量已不足 500 只。 2022 年和 2023 年，禽流感在该保护区蔓延，导致海鸟数量锐减，并蔓延至海狮和海豹等海洋哺乳动物。接下来是厄尔尼诺现象。气候模式的特点是赤道东太平洋的海面温度有数月高于平常。这些温暖的海水将企鹅的主要食物来源凤尾鱼推向更深更远的海域。工业化捕捞作业给幸存的动物带来了更大的压力。

paras.en: Ecologist Susana Cárdenas-Alayza, who has run the Punta San Juan Program in partnership with Cayetano Heredia University, the Peruvian government and American zoos for more than 20 years, is increasingly alarmed. As a scientist, Cárdenas-Alayza says, she is used to dealing with numbers and controlled variables, “but diseases and climate events escape my control.”
paras.zh: 生态学家苏珊娜·卡德纳斯-阿拉扎 (Susana Cárdenas-Alayza) 与卡耶塔诺·埃雷迪亚大学 (Cayetano Heredia University)、秘鲁政府和美国动物园合作运行蓬塔圣胡安计划 (Punta San Juan Program) 20 多年，她越来越感到担忧。卡德纳斯-阿拉扎说，作为一名科学家，她习惯于处理数字和受控变量，“但疾病和气候事件却逃脱了我的控制。”

paras.en: Now, the reserve is facing a new threat: a potential “super” El Niño. Soaring sea surface temperatures are disrupting the cold, fish-rich waters of the Humboldt Current, which flows past the peninsula. When I returned in July, much had changed from my first trip, when streams of penguins lined the cliffs of the reserve. This time I saw only five penguins — and several abandoned nests with cold eggs. When food is scarce, penguins either stop reproducing or leave their nests altogether to search for a more favorable habitat, Cárdenas-Alayza says. They often starve along the way.
paras.zh: 现在，保护区面临着新的威胁：潜在的“超级”厄尔尼诺现象。飙升的海面温度正在扰乱流经半岛的洪堡洋流寒冷且鱼类丰富的水域。当我七月返回时，与我第一次旅行相比，当时的情况发生了很大变化，当时保护区的悬崖上排列着成群的企鹅。这次我只看到了五只企鹅——还有几个废弃的巢穴，里面有冷蛋。卡德纳斯-阿莱扎说，当食物短缺时，企鹅要么停止繁殖，要么完全离开巢穴去寻找更有利的栖息地。他们常常在途中挨饿。

paras.en: The destruction has also been hard on the reserve’s volunteers, who protect the penguins in what Cárdenas-Alayza calls a “living laboratory.” For decades, volunteers from around Peru and the rest of the world have counted birds, recorded their diets and built artificial nests to keep penguin chicks safe. In the summer of 2025, they even launched a “penguin patrol” to safeguard the Humboldts from workers harvesting guano, nitrogen-rich bird droppings essential for agriculture. Wanting to pitch in, the workers built a temporary, half-kilometer-long wall out of sacks of guano to shield the penguins on their daily walk to the sea.
paras.zh: 这次破坏也给保护区的志愿者带来了沉重的打击，他们在卡德纳斯-阿拉萨所说的“活实验室”里保护企鹅。几十年来，来自秘鲁各地和世界其他地方的志愿者统计了鸟类的数量，记录了它们的饮食，并建造了人工巢穴以保证企鹅雏鸟的安全。 2025 年夏天，他们甚至发起了一次“企鹅巡逻”，以保护洪堡家族免受工人收集鸟粪（农业必需的富含氮的鸟粪）的侵害。为了伸出援手，工人们用一袋袋鸟粪搭建了半公里长的临时墙，以保护企鹅每天走向大海。

paras.en: Keeping research going — and morale high — in the emptying ecosystem has been one of the biggest challenges of Cárdenas-Alayza’s career. No one knows how long the current El Niño will last — or when the fish will return.
paras.zh: 在空荡荡的生态系统中保持研究持续进行并保持高昂的士气一直是卡德纳斯-阿拉扎职业生涯中最大的挑战之一。没有人知道当前的厄尔尼诺现象会持续多久，或者鱼什么时候会回来。

paras.en: Nevertheless, Cárdenas-Alayza says she still has hope. Many species in Punta San Juan are philopatric, or loyal to their territory. That means that even when they leave in search of food or other resources, they eventually come back.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，卡德纳斯-阿拉扎说她仍然抱有希望。蓬塔圣胡安的许多物种都是亲民的，或者说忠于自己的领地。这意味着即使它们离开寻找食物或其他资源，它们最终也会回来。

paras.en: Biologist Patricia Majluf, who founded the Punta San Juan Program in 1979, shares one example of resilience: The El Niño event of 1997–98 decimated the reserve’s sea lions and seals. Penguin numbers dropped into the low hundreds. But the animals eventually mounted a remarkable recovery, helped by a major reduction in anchovy fishing quotas in 2006.
paras.zh: 1979 年创立蓬塔圣胡安计划的生物学家帕特里夏·马吉鲁夫 (Patricia Majluf) 分享了一个恢复力的例子：1997-98 年的厄尔尼诺事件导致保护区的海狮和海豹大量死亡。企鹅数量下降至数百只。但在 2006 年凤尾鱼捕捞配额大幅减少的帮助下，这些动物最终取得了显着的恢复。

paras.en: Scientists are busy preparing Punta San Juan for the animals’ return. Cárdenas-Alayza briefed incoming members of Peru’s Congress on the situation in July, and she and her fellow researchers are lobbying hard for stricter fishing quotas. They are also championing a new ecosystem restoration strategy, a collaborative framework that engages fishing communities, companies, students and even local chefs to help the reserve’s animals recover.
paras.zh: 科学家们正忙着为动物的回归做好圣胡安角的准备。卡德纳斯-阿拉扎 (Cárdenas-Alayza) 向即将上任的秘鲁国会议员介绍了 7 月份的情况，她和她的研究同事们正在努力游说，要求实行更严格的捕捞配额。他们还倡导一项新的生态系统恢复战略，这是一个让渔业社区、公司、学生甚至当地厨师参与的协作框架，以帮助保护区的动物恢复。

paras.en: Back in Punta San Juan, Cárdenas-Alayza’s team is pressuring the government to reinforce a protective concrete wall around the reserve. In the meantime, they are trapping invasive species that prey on young birds, such as foxes and rats. They are also developing AI tools to speed data analysis from remote cameras monitoring breeding among the surviving Humboldt penguins.
paras.zh: 回到蓬塔圣胡安，卡德纳斯-阿拉扎的团队正在向政府施压，要求加固保护区周围的混凝土保护墙。与此同时，它们还捕获捕食幼鸟的入侵物种，例如狐狸和老鼠。他们还在开发人工智能工具，以加快对监控幸存洪堡企鹅繁殖情况的远程摄像机的数据分析。

paras.en: Ana Elisa Sotelo’s work on this story was supported by the Pulitzer Center.
paras.zh: 安娜·埃莉莎·索特洛 (Ana Elisa Sotelo) 对这个故事的研究得到了普利策中心的支持。

articles.title: A video of a humpback whale and her dead calf reveals the animals’ bond
articles.author: Melissa Hobson

paras.en: Scientists had a rare view of what could be humpback whale mourning when they spotted a female attending the body of a dead calf.
paras.zh: 当科学家们发现一只雌性座头鲸正在照顾一头死去的小鲸鱼的尸体时，他们罕见地看到了座头鲸可能在哀悼。

paras.en: The sighting suggests that baleen whales may experience grief, marine biologist Olaf Meynecke and rescue boat captain Andrew Mulville report September 16 in Discover Animals.
paras.zh: 海洋生物学家奥拉夫·梅内克 (Olaf Meynecke) 和救援船船长安德鲁·马尔维尔 (Andrew Mulville) 9 月 16 日在《发现动物》杂志上报道称，这一目击事件表明须鲸可能会经历悲伤。

paras.en: Some toothed whales, such as orcas, have been seen spending long periods with dead calves, occasionally carrying them at the surface for days. Such demonstrations of apparent grief are rarely seen in baleen whales. This may be because newborn baleen whales are born without the fat stores that would cause a whale corpse to float. If mothers spend time with dead calves on the seafloor, there’s a very low chance humans would see the interaction. The authors believe this is the first detailed documentation of a humpback attending to a calf after its death.
paras.zh: 人们发现一些齿鲸，例如逆戟鲸，会长时间与死去的小鲸鱼在一起，有时会将它们带到水面数天。这种明显的悲伤表现在须鲸身上很少见。这可能是因为新生的须鲸出生时没有储存使鲸鱼尸体漂浮的脂肪。如果母亲们在海底与死去的小牛一起度过，人类看到这种互动的机会就非常低。作者认为，这是关于座头鲸在小牛死后对其进行照顾的第一份详细记录。

paras.en: In July 2025, Mulville, who works for the Australian marine animal rescue group Sea World Foundation, saw two adult humpback whales (Megaptera novaeangliae) in the water off Palm Beach in Queensland, Australia, and went to check on them. As he approached, he saw some tissue floating on the surface that looked like amniotic membrane — the placental lining that whales shed into the water at birth.
paras.zh: 2025年7月，在澳大利亚海洋动物救援组织海洋世界基金会工作的穆维尔在澳大利亚昆士兰州棕榈滩附近的水域中看到了两只成年座头鲸（Megaptera novaeangliae），并前往查看它们的情况。当他靠近时，他看到一些组织漂浮在表面，看起来像羊膜——鲸鱼出生时脱落到水中的胎盘内壁。

paras.en: On the seafloor, he could see a small newborn calf, less than four meters long. The female “ended up diving down, making eye contact and actually putting her pectoral fin — her arm — over the stillborn and resting next to it,” says Meynecke, from Griffith University in Brisbane, Australia.
paras.zh: 在海底，他看到了一头刚出生的小牛犊，身长不到四米。澳大利亚布里斯班格里菲斯大学的梅内克说，这只雌性“最终潜入水中，进行眼神交流，然后将她的胸鳍——她的手臂——放在死产身上，并在它旁边休息。”

paras.en: Two adult whales, which the researchers believe were the calf’s mother and her male escort, were seen in the same area for two more days. “We can’t prove it, but I’m very certain they were the same whales, which also suggests that this is a prolonged change of behavior … something that we might call mourning or a form of grieving,” he says.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，两只成年鲸鱼是小鲸鱼的母亲和她的雄性护卫，在同一地区又出现了两天。 “我们无法证明这一点，但我非常确定它们是同一头鲸鱼，这也表明这是一种长期的行为变化……我们可以称之为哀悼或悲伤的一种形式，”他说。

paras.en: “It was pretty emotional to observe,” says Meynecke, but he warns against anthropomorphizing and drawing parallels to humans. Remember that “the whale is experiencing their world in a completely different form and shape,” he says. “They have different ways of understanding their environment.”
paras.zh: “观察起来非常情绪化，”梅内克说，但他警告不要将其拟人化并与人类相提并论。请记住，“鲸鱼正在以完全不同的形式和形状体验它们的世界，”他说。 “他们了解环境的方式不同。”

articles.title: Here’s how brain-eating amoebas may infect people
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Some deadly amoebas may be primed to invade the brain.
paras.zh: 一些致命的阿米巴原虫可能准备好入侵大脑。

paras.en: Naegleria fowleri, known widely as the brain-eating amoeba, typically dine on bacteria in ponds. But the amoeba’s meal-seeking skills might make it uniquely suited to crawling up people’s noses and into their brains.
paras.zh: 福氏耐格里阿米巴原虫被广泛称为食脑变形虫，通常以池塘中的细菌为食。但阿米巴原虫的寻食能力可能使其特别适合爬上人们的鼻子并进入他们的大脑。

paras.en: Naegleria amoebas are intrepid explorers, probing nooks and crannies in the lab — and they’re persistent, too. When creeping down narrow passageways, the amoebas charge relentlessly forward, almost never turning back, researchers report September 10 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. “They’re like robots,” says Lillian Fritz-Laylin, a cell biologist at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. “They just go and go and go.”
paras.zh: 变形虫耐格里阿米巴是勇敢的探索者，探索实验室的角落和缝隙——而且它们也很顽强。研究人员于 9 月 10 日在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，当阿米巴原虫爬过狭窄的通道时，它们会毫不留情地向前冲锋，几乎从不回头。 “它们就像机器人，”马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的细胞生物学家莉莲·弗里茨·雷林说。 “他们只是走啊走啊。”

paras.en: Such persistence might help these tiny, single-celled creatures make the marathon journey from the nostrils all the way to the brain. Fritz-Laylin’s work helps flesh out a largely skeletal picture of Naegleria behavior. “We know almost nothing about the basic biology of these organisms,” she says.
paras.zh: 这种坚持可能有助于这些微小的单细胞生物完成从鼻孔一直到大脑的马拉松旅程。弗里茨·雷林的工作有助于充实耐格氏耐格里虫行为的基本框架。 “我们对这些生物体的基本生物学几乎一无所知，”她说。

paras.en: N. fowleri amoebas don’t routinely harm humans. They usually dwell in warm bodies of fresh water, where they squirm through sediment and mind their own business. But on rare occasions, the creatures can be washed up a swimmer’s nose. As the amoebas migrate through the nasal cavity and into the brain, they destroy and eat tissue. Then they begin to reproduce, usually with lethal consequences. The United States typically sees fewer than 10 Naegleria infections each year, often at summer swimming spots, but nearly every one is fatal.
paras.zh: 福氏阿米巴原虫通常不会伤害人类。它们通常居住在温暖的淡水中，在沉积物中蠕动并专注于自己的事情。但在极少数情况下，这些生物可能会被游泳者的鼻子冲走。当变形虫通过鼻腔迁移到大脑时，它们会破坏并吞噬组织。然后它们开始繁殖，通常会带来致命的后果。美国每年通常出现不到 10 例耐格里虫感染，通常发生在夏季游泳场所，但几乎每一种都是致命的。

paras.en: In the lab, Fritz-Laylin’s team tested Naegleria amoebas’ ability to move through different environments. They focused on N. gruberi, a harmless species that shares behaviors with its brain-eating relative. “It’s a lot safer to work with something that can’t kill you,” Fritz-Laylin says.
paras.zh: 在实验室中，Fritz-Laylin 的团队测试了变形虫耐格里阿米巴在不同环境中移动的能力。他们关注的是格鲁伯氏猪笼草，这是一种无害的物种，其行为与其食脑亲戚有共同之处。 “与不会杀死你的东西一起工作要安全得多，”弗里茨·雷林说。

paras.en: The researchers placed the amoebas on glass-bottom dishes containing narrow microchannels and watched them move under a microscope. They squeezed through channels smaller than themselves and seemed to be interested in exploring. When the amoebas encountered a channel opening, they very rarely left it, Fritz-Laylin says. Confinement sometimes sped them up, too. Inside the largest channels tested, the amoebas still zipped along twice as fast as cells on the outside.
paras.zh: 研究人员将阿米巴原虫放在含有狭窄微通道的玻璃底培养皿上，并在显微镜下观察它们的移动。他们挤过比自己还小的通道，似乎有兴趣探索。弗里茨-雷林说，当变形虫遇到通道开口时，它们很少离开它。禁闭有时也会加快他们的速度。在测试的最大通道内，变形虫的移动速度仍然是外部细胞的两倍。

paras.en: Naegleria’s persistence and need for speed may make it unique. The team didn’t observe the same behaviors in a different type of amoeba tested. Such attributes probably make Naegleria well-adapted to hunting bacteria in pond sediments, says Fritz-Laylin, who is also a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator. But those innocent behaviors could also explain N. fowleri’s dark side. Put one at “the wrong place at the wrong time,” she says, “and it can cause devastating infection.”
paras.zh: 耐格里虫的坚持和对速度的需求可能使其独一无二。研究小组在测试的不同类型阿米巴原虫中没有观察到相同的行为。霍华德休斯医学研究所研究员弗里茨-莱林说，这些特性可能使耐格里氏耐格里虫非常适合捕猎池塘沉积物中的细菌。但这些无辜的行为也可以解释福氏猪笼草的阴暗面。她说，“在错误的时间、错误的地点，可能会导致毁灭性的感染。”

articles.title: Scientists Find a Surprising Link Between Cats And Happiness Across 93 Countries
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: If you're looking for a boost of household happiness, then you might want to consider getting yourself a cat.
paras.zh: 如果您正在寻求提升家庭幸福感，那么您可能需要考虑养一只猫。

paras.en: In a new study published in PLOS One, an international team of researchers analyzed publicly available data across 93 countries to examine the relationship between happiness scores, domestic cat density, and infection rates of Toxoplasma gondii – the parasite that affects as many as 1 in 3 people and which felines are the primary host of.
paras.zh: 在 PLOS One 上发表的一项新研究中，一个国际研究小组分析了 93 个国家的公开数据，以研究幸福评分、家猫密度和弓形虫感染率之间的关系。弓形虫是一种寄生虫，影响多达三分之一的人，猫科动物是其主要宿主。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to see if having a cat made a difference to happiness, and whether the risk of parasite infection affected that in any way.
paras.zh: 研究人员想看看养猫是否会对幸福感产生影响，以及寄生虫感染的风险是否会以任何方式影响幸福感。

paras.en: While T. gondii is usually harmless and symptomless for most people, it can cause problems in more vulnerable groups, and has been linked to anxiety, depression, and schizophrenia.
paras.zh: 虽然弓形虫通常对大多数人无害且无症状，但它可能会给更脆弱的群体带来问题，并与焦虑、抑郁和精神分裂症有关。

paras.en: Wealth was also included as it's often one of the first factors people consider when it comes to leading a happy and comfortable life.
paras.zh: 财富也被包括在内，因为它通常是人们在过上幸福舒适的生活时首先考虑的因素之一。

paras.en: "What we found is that countries with more cats tended to report higher levels of happiness, while countries with higher exposure to Toxoplasma gondii tended to report lower levels of happiness," say the study authors in a press release.
paras.zh: 该研究的作者在一份新闻稿中表示：“我们发现，猫较多的国家往往幸福感较高，而接触弓形虫较多的国家幸福感较低。”

paras.en: Those apparently conflicting results need some picking apart. Certain countries may have had a disproportionate impact on the results, the researchers suggest.
paras.zh: 这些明显相互矛盾的结果需要一些区分。研究人员表示，某些国家可能对结果产生了不成比例的影响。

paras.en: China, for instance, had a relatively high happiness score despite a lower cat density than most nations.
paras.zh: 例如，尽管中国的猫密度低于大多数国家，但中国的幸福感得分相对较高。

paras.en: One of the more surprising wrinkles in the data was that countries with more cats tended to have lower levels of T. gondii exposure.
paras.zh: 数据中更令人惊讶的问题之一是，猫较多的国家往往弓形虫暴露水平较低。

paras.en: Cats aren't the only way humans can be infected by this parasite, but you would expect the association to be in the other direction.
paras.zh: 猫并不是人类感染这种寄生虫的唯一途径，但你可能会认为这种联系是相反的。

paras.en: "Of course, these are associations at the country level, so we cannot say that having more cats makes people happier or that Toxoplasma makes people less happy, but the patterns are interesting enough to deserve further investigation," say the study authors.
paras.zh: 研究作者说：“当然，这些都是国家层面的关联，所以我们不能说养更多的猫让人们更快乐，或者弓形虫让人们不那么快乐，但这些模式很有趣，值得进一步研究。”

paras.en: Then there's the consideration that wealthier countries may make people more likely to own cats and have better access to vet care.
paras.zh: 还有一个考虑因素是，较富裕的国家可能会让人们更有可能养猫并有更好的机会获得兽医护理。

paras.en: Felines in richer countries are more likely to be kept indoors, get regular check-ups at the vet, and eat commercial cat food.
paras.zh: 富裕国家的猫科动物更有可能被关在室内，定期去看兽医检查，并吃商业猫粮。

paras.en: The findings suggest that biological and ecological factors can play a role in finding that much-desired feeling of happiness, factors which aren't typically included in studies.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，生物和生态因素可以在寻找人们渴望的幸福感方面发挥作用，而这些因素通常不会包含在研究中。

paras.en: "This goes against the simple assumption that having more cats necessarily means greater parasite exposure and suggests that factors such as pets management, sanitation, and socioeconomic conditions may be important," says biologist Javier I. Borráz-León, from the National Institute of Psychiatry Ramón de la Fuente Muñiz in Mexico.
paras.zh: “这违背了一个简单的假设，即养更多的猫必然意味着更多的寄生虫暴露，并表明宠物管理、卫生条件和社会经济条件等因素可能很重要，”墨西哥拉蒙德拉富恩特穆尼兹国家精神病学研究所的生物学家哈维尔·博拉兹-莱昂说。

paras.en: How happy (or otherwise) populations are can have very tangible effects on public health, which is why studies like this are so important.
paras.zh: 人口的幸福程度（或其他方面）会对公共健康产生非常明显的影响，这就是为什么这样的研究如此重要。

paras.en: When people are stressed, anxious, and unhappy, they're less productive, more vulnerable, and more likely to need treatment and care from other people.
paras.zh: 当人们感到压力、焦虑和不快乐时，他们的生产力就会降低，更加脆弱，并且更有可能需要其他人的治疗和护理。

paras.en: Now we know that having a cat around could lead to a boost in contentment and well-being, adding to other recent cat and pet discoveries – including research that showed animal companions may help to slow down cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 现在我们知道，有一只猫在身边可以提高满足感和幸福感，这也增加了最近对猫和宠物的其他发现——包括表明动物伙伴可能有助于减缓认知能力下降的研究。

paras.en: To take the research further, future studies could track cat owners and non-cat owners on an individual basis, rather than at the country level.
paras.zh: 为了进一步开展研究，未来的研究可以在个人基础上而不是在国家层面上追踪养猫者和非养猫者。

paras.en: That should reveal more about the relationship between cats and happiness and how it might change over time, in combination with other factors.
paras.zh: 这应该能更多地揭示猫和幸福之间的关系，以及它如何随着时间的推移，结合其他因素而发生变化。

paras.en: "Future studies of happiness at the national level should integrate both socioeconomic and biological perspectives and include longitudinal and interdisciplinary approaches to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and processes," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“未来在国家层面上对幸福的研究应该整合社会经济和生物学的观点，并包括纵向和跨学科的方法来阐明潜在的机制和过程。”

paras.en: The research has been published in PLOS One.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 PLOS One 上。

articles.title: After 25 Years, Physicists Can Finally Measure The 'Other' Kind of Quantum Entanglement
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Quantum entanglement is one of the most cognitively jarring disconnects between the quantum domain and the macroscopic world.
paras.zh: 量子纠缠是量子领域与宏观世界之间最令人震惊的认知脱节之一。

paras.en: When fundamental particles such as electrons or photons are entangled, they share a quantum identity and cannot be described as individual entities; they exist in a superposition with no fixed state until at least one is measured.
paras.zh: 当电子或光子等基本粒子纠缠在一起时，它们共享量子身份，不能被描述为单独的实体；它们以叠加的形式存在，没有固定状态，直到至少有一个被测量为止。

paras.en: This transcends physical distance, so a quantum-entangled coin flip on Earth would produce an instantaneous and commensurate result on Mars.
paras.zh: 这超越了物理距离，因此地球上的量子纠缠硬币翻转将在火星上产生瞬时且相应的结果。

paras.en: Of course, these results are random and transmit no information, squashing hopes for faster-than-light communication or an intricate terrestrial-Martian coin-flip cheating ring.
paras.zh: 当然，这些结果是随机的，并且不传输任何信息，从而粉碎了对超光速通信或复杂的地球-火星抛硬币作弊圈的希望。

paras.en: Still, entanglement is critical for quantum information technologies; we just need to increase how many particles we entangle and our ability to measure these systems.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，纠缠对于量子信息技术仍然至关重要。我们只需要增加纠缠粒子的数量以及测量这些系统的能力。

paras.en: To that end, physicists from Kyoto University and Hiroshima University have pulled us one or a few steps closer to our looming quantum future in a landmark study that determined the configuration of multi-particle entangled states, starting with three photons.
paras.zh: 为此，京都大学和广岛大学的物理学家在一项具有里程碑意义的研究中使我们离迫在眉睫的量子未来更近了一步，该研究从三个光子开始确定了多粒子纠缠态的配置。

paras.en: In their paper, published in Science Advances in September 2025, physicists finally reported a new technique to perform measurements of the so-called W-state entanglement types.
paras.zh: 在 2025 年 9 月发表在《科学进展》上的论文中，物理学家最终报告了一种测量所谓 W 态纠缠类型的新技术。

paras.en: Previously, scientists measured Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, the well-known and fundamental 'vanilla ice cream' of multi-particle entanglement systems.
paras.zh: 此前，科学家测量了格林伯格-霍恩-蔡林格 (GHZ) 态，这是多粒子纠缠系统中众所周知的基本“香草冰淇淋”。

paras.en: "More than 25 years after the initial proposal concerning the entangled measurement for GHZ states, we have finally obtained the entangled measurement for the W state as well, with genuine experimental demonstration for 3-photon W states," explains Shigeki Takeuchi, a quantum information researcher.
paras.zh: 量子信息研究员 Shigeki Takeuchi 解释道：“在最初提出 GHZ 态纠缠测量的 25 年多后，我们终于也获得了 W 态的纠缠测量，并对 3 光子 W 态进行了真正的实验演示。”

paras.en: Importantly, particle entanglement is often measured using a technique known as quantum tomography. It works kind of like the X-ray computed tomography that reveals our bodies' skeletal secrets.
paras.zh: 重要的是，粒子纠缠通常使用量子断层扫描技术来测量。它的工作原理有点像 X 射线计算机断层扫描，可以揭示我们身体的骨骼秘密。

paras.en: It involves taking many measurements, and then putting these 'slices' together into a coherent image.
paras.zh: 它涉及进行多次测量，然后将这些“切片”组合在一起形成连贯的图像。

paras.en: But this can be inefficient and tricky, introducing two practical bottlenecks.
paras.zh: 但这可能效率低下且棘手，会引入两个实际瓶颈。

paras.en: First, scientists must create many identical entangled systems, because measuring (observing) their properties snaps them out of their entangled states.
paras.zh: 首先，科学家必须创建许多相同的纠缠系统，因为测量（观察）它们的特性可以使它们摆脱纠缠态。

paras.en: Second, the measurements required to reconstruct an entangled state exponentially rise with the number of entangled particles.
paras.zh: 其次，重建纠缠态所需的测量随着纠缠粒子的数量呈指数增长。

paras.en: The researchers managed to sidestep these issues with a one-shot measurement that determined the entire entangled system in a single step.
paras.zh: 研究人员设法通过一次性测量来回避这些问题，该测量一步即可确定整个纠缠系统。

paras.en: They did so using a discrete Fourier transform (DFT) optical circuit device of their own making, which acted as an advanced interferometer.
paras.zh: 他们使用自己制造的离散傅里叶变换（DFT）光路装置来实现这一点，该装置充当先进的干涉仪。

paras.en: In other words, they injected three photons of known polarization into this device, which split them along different paths and then crashed them back into each other, to see how the peaks and valleys of their wave functions lined up, either combining or canceling out.
paras.zh: 换句话说，他们将三个已知偏振的光子注入到这个装置中，装置将它们沿着不同的路径分开，然后将它们撞回彼此，以观察它们的波函数的波峰和波谷如​​何排列，或者组合，或者抵消。

paras.en: This allowed the researchers to explore the W state's "cyclic shift symmetry," which is a bit like a system's fingerprint based on the symmetry of its quantum properties.
paras.zh: 这使得研究人员能够探索 W 态的“循环移位对称性”，这有点像基于其量子特性对称性的系统指纹。

paras.en: The "cyclic shift" part means that the entangled system's structural description does not change when its individual photons are shifted in a cyclical fashion.
paras.zh: “循环移位”部分意味着当单个光子以循环方式移位时，纠缠系统的结构描述不会改变。

paras.en: Imagine a group of people sitting in a circle around a campfire. Suddenly, each of them stands up and shifts over one seat to the left (who knows why, perhaps they're part of an esoteric Borg-like hivemind that has not lost its ancestral fascination with flames).
paras.zh: 想象一下一群人围着篝火围坐一圈。突然，他们每个人都站了起来，向左移了一个座位（谁知道为什么，也许他们是深奥的博格式蜂巢思维的一部分，并没有失去其祖先对火焰的迷恋）。

paras.en: As a result, the cyclically shifted Borg circle looks the same.
paras.zh: 结果，循环移位的博格圆看起来是一样的。

paras.en: And thus, the researchers revealed an averaged measurement discrimination fidelity (MDF) of 0.871 ± 0.039.
paras.zh: 因此，研究人员发现平均测量辨别保真度 (MDF) 为 0.871 ± 0.039。

paras.en: They correctly identified the W state condition 87 percent of the time, comfortably exceeding the mathematical threshold of 66.7 percent (two-thirds) to demonstrate that three-particle entanglement measurement has been achieved, thereby proving the efficacy of their methodology.
paras.zh: 他们在 87% 的时间内正确识别了 W 状态条件，轻松超过了 66.7%（三分之二）的数学阈值，证明了三粒子纠缠测量已经实现，从而证明了其方法的有效性。

paras.en: The team attributes the shortfall to imperfections in photon preparation and the measurement setup itself.
paras.zh: 该团队将这一缺陷归因于光子准备和测量设置本身的缺陷。

paras.en: "We believe that these results represent an important milestone toward a wider application of multi-qubit entangled measurements in photonic quantum computation, quantum communication, and sensing," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们相信，这些结果代表了多量子位纠缠测量在光子量子计算、量子通信和传感领域更广泛应用的一个重要里程碑。”

paras.en: Accordingly, this work helps open the door – hopefully not a quantum door that's both open and closed at the same time, i.e., Schrödinger's stubbed toe – for quantum applications in computing and cryptography.
paras.zh: 因此，这项工作有助于为计算和密码学中的量子应用打开一扇门——希望不是同时打开和关闭的量子门，即薛定谔的脚趾。

paras.en: The team now plans to develop on-chip photonic quantum circuits for these entangled measurements.
paras.zh: 该团队现在计划开发用于这些纠缠测量的片上光子量子电路。

paras.en: Given the gaping technological maw of quantum computing, these advances could come together to improve life-saving drug research or personalized healthcare strategies, for example.
paras.zh: 例如，考虑到量子计算技术的巨大进步，这些进步可以结合起来改善救生药物研究或个性化医疗保健策略。

paras.en: They could also make our Pizza Hut rewards points accounts more secure than ever – unless a pepperoni-hungry hacker also has quantum computing access.
paras.zh: 它们还可以使我们的必胜客奖励积分账户比以往任何时候都更加安全——除非渴望意大利辣香肠的黑客也拥有量子计算访问权限。

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: Skulls of Civilians Buried Around Egypt's First Kings Reveal Evidence of Human Sacrifice
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: You might have read somewhere that in ancient Egypt, royalty were often buried with people sacrificed to serve them in the afterlife, but archaeologists aren't actually so sure about that.
paras.zh: 您可能在某处读到，在古埃及，皇室成员经常与在来世为他们服务的牺牲品一起埋葬，但考古学家实际上对此并不太确定。

paras.en: When British Egyptologist Flinders Petrie excavated graves surrounding the tombs of ancient Egyptian First Dynasty kings in the 1920s, he found the remains of many more people – hundreds, in some cases.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 20 年代，英国埃及古物学家弗林德斯·皮特里 (Flinders Petrie) 在古埃及第一王朝国王陵墓周围挖掘坟墓时，发现了更多人的遗骸，有的甚至有数百人。

paras.en: At the time, he suspected the people in these satellite graves could have been sacrificed shortly after each king's death, in what is known as a retainer sacrifice.
paras.zh: 当时，他怀疑这些卫星坟墓中的人可能在每位国王去世后不久就被牺牲了，这就是所谓的家臣祭祀。

paras.en: But Petrie was unable to find evidence for how these people died, a gap that has left this theory open to doubt.
paras.zh: 但皮特里无法找到这些人如何死亡的证据，这一空白使这一理论受到质疑。

paras.en: Archaeologist Roselyn Campbell, of Purdue University in the US, has been revisiting Petrie's work with a modern forensic approach, confirming that 18 of the 46 skulls Petrie preserved and brought back to England show signs of potentially lethal injuries.
paras.zh: 美国普渡大学的考古学家 Roselyn Campbell 一直在用现代法医方法重新审视 Petrie 的工作，确认 Petrie 保存并带回英国的 46 个头骨中，有 18 个显示出潜在致命伤害的迹象。

paras.en: She presents her findings in a new paper, published today in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology.
paras.zh: 她在今天发表在环境考古学前沿的一篇新论文中介绍了她的发现。

paras.en: These skulls were unearthed from around the royal funerary complexes at Umm el-Qaab in ancient Abydos, where they were interred near ancient Egypt's first kings. These First Dynasty leaders ruled from around 3078 to 2900 BCE.
paras.zh: 这些头骨是从古阿比多斯乌姆卡布的皇家墓葬建筑群周围出土的，它们被埋葬在古埃及第一代国王附近。这些第一王朝领导人的统治时间约为公元前 3078 年至 2900 年。

paras.en: Some of the graves surrounding the royal burials were marked with names and official titles, identifying them as lower- or mid-level officials, or artisans.
paras.zh: 皇家墓葬周围的一些坟墓上刻有姓名和官方头衔，表明他们是中低级官员或工匠。

paras.en: "Each subsidiary burial was a simple chamber in a row of dozens of others," says Campbell.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔说：“每个附属墓葬都是一排简单的墓室，与其他几十个墓室相连。”

paras.en: "Some people had a simple coffin. Most people had a few grave goods, like ceramic vessels, and many graves also included small objects like copper tools, projectile points, or small ivory figurines."
paras.zh: “有些人有一个简单的棺材。大多数人有一些随葬品，如陶瓷器皿，许多坟墓还包括一些小物品，如铜工具、弹头或小象牙雕像。”

paras.en: Campbell has been re-analyzing the skulls of these ancient Egyptian civilians for several years.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔多年来一直在重新分析这些古埃及平民的头骨。

paras.en: Linear fractures across the skullcap are the most common injuries she has found – a kind of damage that is usually caused by flat, wide objects.
paras.zh: 头盖骨上的线性骨折是她发现的最常见的损伤——这种损伤通常是由扁平、宽阔的物体造成的。

paras.en: In a few of the skulls, Campbell also found sharp force injuries, including "a penetrative injury to the side of the head" and "a chopping injury to the eye".
paras.zh: 在一些头骨中，坎贝尔还发现了锐器损伤，包括“头部侧面的穿透伤”和“眼睛的砍伤”。

paras.en: "While it is certainly possible that some individuals may have died peacefully from some other cause and been buried around the royal funerary complexes, it is also clear that many of these individuals did experience perimortem trauma of some kind," Campbell writes.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔写道：“虽然有些人可能因其他原因平静地去世，并被埋葬在皇家墓地周围，但很明显，其中许多人确实经历了某种临死前的创伤。”

paras.en: In other words, it's quite likely that these subjects were killed deliberately, by traumatic blows to the head.
paras.zh: 换句话说，这些对象很可能是被故意杀害的，即头部遭受创伤性打击。

paras.en: "Petrie believed that the closure of so many graves at once made individual interments after natural deaths unlikely, and the apparently hasty closure of so many tombs along with the identity of officials associated in some way with the royal court led him to conclude that these burials probably represented retainer sacrifice," Campbell writes.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔写道：“皮特里认为，同时关闭如此多的坟墓使得自然死亡后不太可能进行个人安葬，而且如此多的坟墓明显仓促关闭，再加上与王室有某种联系的官员的身份，使他得出结论，这些墓葬可能代表了家臣的牺牲。”

paras.en: Her findings lend further credence to Petrie's theory: that the people in these subsidiary burials may have been sacrificed when their king died, with the belief that they would serve their ruler in the afterlife.
paras.zh: 她的发现进一步证实了皮特里的理论：这些附属墓葬中的人可能在国王去世时被牺牲，相信他们会在来世为他们的统治者服务。

paras.en: If so, it also seems this practice started very early in the culture of ancient Egypt.
paras.zh: 如果是这样，这种做法似乎在古埃及文化中很早就开始了。

paras.en: "Some retainers might have volunteered to die to achieve eternal life or honor, others may have been chosen or even forced," Campbell suggests.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔表示：“一些家臣可能自愿死去以获得永生或荣誉，其他人可能是被选择甚至被迫的。”

paras.en: "If I had unlimited resources, I would love to figure out where the bodies of these individuals might be and analyze them!
paras.zh: “如果我有无限的资源，我很想弄清楚这些人的尸体可能在哪里并对其进行分析！

paras.en: "Still, this study shows how much new information about the past can be revealed when we revisit previous data armed with updated methods and knowledge, even for datasets that are incomplete and imperfect like this one."
paras.zh: “不过，这项研究表明，当我们用更新的方法和知识重新审视以前的数据时，即使对于像这样不完整和不完美的数据集，也可以揭示多少关于过去的新信息。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《环境考古学前沿》上。

articles.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging

paras.en: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
paras.zh: 你的肠道细菌可能会揭示你的大脑衰老的速度

paras.en: Your gut bacteria may offer an early clue to how quickly your brain is aging.
paras.zh: 您的肠道细菌可能会为您的大脑衰老速度提供早期线索。

paras.en: - University of California - Los Angeles Health Sciences
paras.zh: - 加州大学洛杉矶分校健康科学学院

paras.en: - A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood. The findings suggest that biological signs of brain aging may appear decades before obvious symptoms and could eventually make the gut a target for prevention.
paras.zh: - 加州大学洛杉矶分校的一项研究表明，大脑衰老速度加快与特定的肠道细菌和化学副产品有关，而看起来较老的大脑也与记忆力、注意力和情绪较差有关。研究结果表明，大脑衰老的生物学迹象可能比明显症状早几十年出现，最终可能使肠道成为预防的目标。

paras.en: A new UCLA study suggests that the pace of brain aging may be connected to bacteria in the gut and the chemical compounds they produce. The findings offer a new look at biological changes that may begin long before noticeable problems with memory or thinking appear.
paras.zh: 加州大学洛杉矶分校的一项新研究表明，大脑衰老的速度可能与肠道细菌及其产生的化合物有关。这些发现为生物学变化提供了新的视角，这些变化可能早在明显的记忆或思维问题出现之前就开始了。

paras.en: Scientists have used brain scans for years to estimate a person's "brain age," which can differ from chronological age. Previous research has found that when the brain appears older than expected, that pattern can be associated with poorer memory, weaker thinking skills and changes in mood.
paras.zh: 多年来，科学家们一直使用脑部扫描来估计一个人的“大脑年龄”，这可能与实际年龄不同。先前的研究发现，当大脑看起来比预期更老时，这种模式可能与记忆力较差、思维能力较弱和情绪变化有关。

paras.en: Most earlier studies, however, focused on older adults or people who already had neurological conditions. That left an important question unanswered: does an older looking brain also matter in younger, generally healthy adults?
paras.zh: 然而，大多数早期研究都集中在老年人或已经患有神经系统疾病的人身上。这就留下了一个重要的问题没有得到解答：看起来较老的大脑对于年轻、总体健康的成年人来说也很重要吗？

paras.en: In a new study published in the journal eBioMedicine, UCLA Health researchers examined brain scans from nearly 1,500 adults divided across three separate groups.
paras.zh: 在 eBioMedicine 杂志上发表的一项新研究中，加州大学洛杉矶分校健康中心的研究人员检查了分为三个不同组的近 1,500 名成年人的脑部扫描。

paras.en: The team used a scanning approach that measures how different areas of the brain communicate with one another while a person is at rest. Researchers then created a computer model that estimated each person's age based on those communication patterns.
paras.zh: 研究小组使用一种扫描方法来测量一个人休息时大脑不同区域如何相互沟通。然后研究人员创建了一个计算机模型，根据这些沟通模式估计每个人的年龄。

paras.en: They compared the estimated brain age with each participant's actual age. The difference between the two became what the researchers called the Brain Aging Index (BAI).
paras.zh: 他们将估计的大脑年龄与每个参与者的实际年龄进行了比较。两者之间的差异被研究人员称为大脑老化指数（BAI）。

paras.en: Older-Looking Brains Were Linked to Memory and Mood
paras.zh: 看起来更老的大脑与记忆和情绪有关

paras.en: Across all three groups, participants whose brains appeared older than their chronological age generally performed worse on tests of working memory and executive function. Those abilities help people hold information in mind, stay focused, plan, and organize.
paras.zh: 在所有三组中，大脑看起来比实际年龄更老的参与者在工作记忆和执行功能测试中通常表现较差。这些能力帮助人们牢记信息、保持专注、计划和组织。

paras.en: People with a higher Brain Aging Index also reported more symptoms of depression. The patterns repeatedly involved brain regions associated with memory and self-referential thought, or the mental processes people use when thinking about themselves and their own experiences.
paras.zh: 大脑老化指数较高的人也报告了更多的抑郁症状。这些模式反复涉及与记忆和自我参照思维相关的大脑区域，或者人们在思考自己和自己的经历时使用的心理过程。

paras.en: For one of the study groups, the researchers also examined stool samples to see whether differences in brain aging were connected to changes in the gut.
paras.zh: 对于其中一个研究组，研究人员还检查了粪便样本，看看大脑衰老的差异是否与肠道的变化有关。

paras.en: They found that a higher Brain Aging Index was associated with specific gut bacteria and several metabolic byproducts. These included certain fat molecules, a cholesterol-related compound and lower levels of a hormone called estetrol.
paras.zh: 他们发现较高的大脑老化指数与特定的肠道细菌和几种代谢副产物有关。其中包括某些脂肪分子、一种与胆固醇相关的化合物和较低水平的雌四醇激素。

paras.en: The pathways connected with these biological signals involved the immune system, blood vessel function, communication between brain cells and the processes cells use to produce energy.
paras.zh: 与这些生物信号相关的通路涉及免疫系统、血管功能、脑细胞之间的通讯以及细胞用来产生能量的过程。

paras.en: Signs of Brain Aging May Appear Decades Early
paras.zh: 大脑老化的迹象可能会提前几十年出现

paras.en: "Brain aging doesn't suddenly begin when we get older, but the biological signals may be detectable decades earlier," said the study's senior author Dr. Arpana Church, co-director of the Goodman-Luskin Microbiome Center at UCLA Health. "By linking these early brain changes with the gut microbiome and its metabolites, we are beginning to identify pathways that could ultimately help us understand who may be at risk and, importantly, where we might intervene to support healthier brain aging. This ultimately opens the door to exploring whether targeting gut health could one day support healthier brain aging."
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者、加州大学洛杉矶分校健康中心古德曼-拉斯金微生物组中心联席主任阿帕纳·丘奇博士说：“大脑衰老不会随着我们年龄的增长而突然开始，但生物信号可能会在几十年前就被检测到。” “通过将这些早期大脑变化与肠道微生物组及其代谢物联系起来，我们开始确定最终可以帮助我们了解谁可能面临风险的途径，更重要的是，我们可以在哪里进行干预以支持更健康的大脑衰老。这最终为探索以肠道健康为目标是否有朝一日支持更健康的大脑衰老打开了大门。”

paras.en: Church said the findings may eventually help researchers identify people at greater risk of cognitive or mood-related decline earlier in life. They also raise the possibility that the gut could become a target for future strategies designed to support brain health and prevention earlier in life.
paras.zh: 丘奇说，这些发现最终可能会帮助研究人员识别出在生命早期出现认知或情绪相关衰退风险更大的人。他们还提出了一种可能性，即肠道可能成为未来旨在支持大脑健康和生命早期预防的策略的目标。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of California - Los Angeles Health Sciences. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州大学洛杉矶分校健康科学分校提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Kanhao Zhao, Gabriel A. Vignolle, Jennifer S. Labus, Emeran A. Mayer, Allison Vaughan, Marika Dy, Priten Vora, Ming W. Hung, Keith Vossel, Chris Gill, Daniele Del Rio, Catherine Stanton, R. Paul Ross, John F. Cryan, Rima Kaddurah-Daouk, Yu Zhang, Arpana Church. Brain-gut crosstalk associated with brain ageing in young and mid-life adults: a multicohort cross-sectional study. eBioMedicine, 2026; 132: 106468 DOI: 10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106468
paras.zh: - 赵侃豪、Gabriel A. Vignolle、Jennifer S. Labus、Emeran A. Mayer、Allison Vaughan、Marika Dy、Priten Vora、Ming W. Hung、Keith Vossel、Chris Gill、Daniele Del Rio、Catherine Stanton、R. Paul Ross、John F. Cryan、Rima Kaddurah-Daouk、Yu 张，Arpana Church。与年轻人和中年成年人大脑衰老相关的脑肠串扰：一项多队列横断面研究。电子生物医学，2026； 132：106468 DOI：10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106468

articles.title: Easing constipation: A 20-minute walk can get your gut moving almost immediately

paras.en: Easing constipation: A 20-minute walk can get your gut moving almost immediately
paras.zh: 缓解便秘：步行 20 分钟几乎可以立即让肠道蠕动

paras.en: - Researchers found that just 20 minutes of comfortable walking can rapidly stimulate the gut. Within one to two minutes after exercise, bowel sounds became stronger, more frequent, and lasted longer, suggesting increased intestinal movement. The boost was brief, fading within a few minutes, but it may help explain why walking can provide relief from constipation.
paras.zh: - 研究人员发现，只需 20 分钟舒适的步行即可迅速刺激肠道。运动后一到两分钟内，肠鸣音变得更强、更频繁、持续时间更长，表明肠道运动增加。这种促进作用是短暂的，几分钟内就会消失，但这可能有助于解释为什么步行可以缓解便秘。

paras.en: Constipation is one of the most common digestive problems, affecting people across age groups and backgrounds. Beyond causing bloating, straining, and infrequent bowel movements, it can also interfere with daily life by increasing stress, reducing productivity, and lowering overall quality of life. When constipation becomes persistent, it may also contribute to complications such as hemorrhoids, cardiovascular strain, and an increased risk of colorectal problems.
paras.zh: 便秘是最常见的消化问题之一，影响各个年龄段和背景的人们。除了引起腹胀、用力和排便不频繁之外，它还会增加压力、降低生产力和降低整体生活质量，从而干扰日常生活。当便秘持续存在时，还可能导致痔疮、心血管紧张等并发症，并增加结直肠问题的风险。

paras.en: Despite how widespread it is, constipation is often ignored or left untreated until symptoms become difficult to manage. That makes it important to better understand both what causes sluggish bowel function and which strategies can help restore normal digestion.
paras.zh: 尽管便秘很普遍，但它常常被忽视或得不到治疗，直到症状变得难以控制。因此，更好地了解导致肠道功能迟缓的原因以及哪些策略可以帮助恢复正常消化非常重要。

paras.en: Physical activity is one of the simplest approaches commonly recommended for constipation. People who are more active generally tend to have healthier bowel function, while prolonged inactivity is often associated with slower digestion.
paras.zh: 体力活动是通常推荐的治疗便秘的最简单方法之一。活动较多的人通常肠道功能更健康，而长期不活动通常会导致消化速度减慢。

paras.en: Exactly why movement helps, however, is not fully understood. Much of the previous research has examined the effects of regular exercise over longer periods. Scientists know much less about what happens inside the digestive system immediately after a person starts moving.
paras.zh: 然而，运动为何有效的具体原因尚不完全清楚。之前的大部分研究都考察了长期定期锻炼的影响。科学家们对人开始运动后消化系统内部发生的情况知之甚少。

paras.en: Understanding those rapid changes could help explain why even a relatively short walk may help stimulate bowel function.
paras.zh: 了解这些快速变化有助于解释为什么即使相对较短的步行也可能有助于刺激肠道功能。

paras.en: Researchers from Fujita Health University set out to investigate how quickly physical activity can influence gut motility in healthy adults. In their study, published in Scientific Reports, the team used bowel sounds (BS) as a non-invasive way to monitor intestinal activity.
paras.zh: 藤田健康大学的研究人员着手研究身体活动对健康成年人肠道蠕动的影响有多快。在发表在《科学报告》上的研究中，研究小组使用肠鸣音（BS）作为监测肠道活动的非侵入性方法。

paras.en: Bowel sounds are produced as gas and fluid move through the intestines. Because those movements are related to the contractions that propel digestive contents through the gut, the sounds can provide clues about gut motility. By recording them before and after exercise, the researchers were able to examine how rapidly the digestive system responded to walking.
paras.zh: 当气体和液体穿过肠道时会产生肠鸣音。由于这些运动与推动消化内容物通过肠道的收缩有关，因此这些声音可以提供有关肠道蠕动的线索。通过在运动前后记录它们，研究人员能够检查消化系统对步行的反应有多快。

paras.en: The study included 21 healthy young adults. At the beginning of the experiment, each participant lay quietly while the researchers recorded one minute of baseline BS using an electronic stethoscope and advanced signal-processing software.
paras.zh: 该研究包括 21 名健康的年轻人。实验开始时，每个参与者安静地躺着，研究人员使用电子听诊器和先进的信号处理软件记录一分钟的基线BS。

paras.en: The participants then walked on a treadmill for 20 minutes at a comfortable, self-selected pace. After the walk, they returned to a lying position while the researchers recorded BS at several points during the following 15 minutes.
paras.zh: 然后，参与者以自己选择的舒适配速在跑步机上行走 20 分钟。步行结束后，他们恢复躺卧姿势，同时研究人员在接下来的 15 分钟内记录了多个时间点的 BS。

paras.en: Gut motility was evaluated using three measurements. These included the Sound Index (SI), which measures the total amplitude of sound activity; the percentage of recording time during which BS could be detected; and the number of separate BS events occurring each minute.
paras.zh: 使用三个测量值来评估肠道蠕动。其中包括声音指数（SI），它测量声音活动的总振幅；可以检测到 BS 的记录时间百分比；以及每分钟发生的单独 BS 事件的数量。

paras.en: Within one to two minutes after participants finished walking, all three measures had risen significantly compared with their resting levels. The amplitude of the bowel sounds nearly doubled, the sounds were present during a much larger share of the recordings, and the number of individual sounds per minute also increased.
paras.zh: 参与者完成步行后一到两分钟内，所有三项指标均较静息水平显着上升。肠鸣音的振幅几乎增加了一倍，在更大比例的录音中出现了声音，并且每分钟的单个声音的数量也增加了。

paras.en: The effect did not last long. The increases diminished within two to three minutes. Still, the speed of the response showed that even light activity can produce an immediate and measurable increase in gut motility.
paras.zh: 效果并没有持续多久。增加在两到三分钟内减少。尽管如此，反应速度表明，即使是轻微的活动也能立即产生可测量的肠道蠕动增加。

paras.en: A Possible Explanation for Walking and Constipation Relief
paras.zh: 步行和缓解便秘的可能解释

paras.en: The findings may help clarify why walking is so often recommended for people dealing with constipation.
paras.zh: 这些发现可能有助于阐明为什么经常建议患有便秘的人步行。

paras.en: Professor Yohei Otaka, senior author of the study, shares, "Walking can serve as an effective, immediate tool for stimulating bowel function. The findings also point to potential underlying mechanisms, such as changes in autonomic nervous system activity or reflexes triggered by the body's natural oscillations during movement."
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者 Yohei Otaka 教授表示：“步行可以作为刺激肠道功能的一种有效、直接的工具。研究结果还指出了潜在的潜在机制，例如运动过程中身体自然振荡引发的自主神经系统活动或反射的变化。”

paras.en: The autonomic nervous system helps regulate many automatic functions in the body, including digestion. The physical motion created while walking could also contribute by triggering reflexes that encourage the intestines to become more active.
paras.zh: 自主神经系统有助于调节身体的许多自动功能，包括消化。步行时产生的身体运动也可以通过触发反射来促进肠道变得更加活跃。

paras.en: The research team also included Professor Shigeo Tanabe (Graduate School of Health Sciences, Fujita Health University) and Kento Katagiri (Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, School of Medicine, Fujita Health University), who contributed to study design, analysis, and manuscript preparation.
paras.zh: 研究团队还包括 Shigeo Tanabe 教授（藤田保健大学健康科学研究生院）和 Kento Katagiri（藤田保健大学医学院康复医学系），他们为研究设计、分析和手稿准备做出了贡献。

paras.en: Bowel Sounds Could Offer a New Research Tool
paras.zh: 肠鸣音可以提供新的研究工具

paras.en: Beyond the effects of walking itself, the findings suggest that BS analysis could become a useful non-invasive method for studying gastrointestinal function and constipation.
paras.zh: 除了步行本身的影响之外，研究结果表明 BS 分析可能成为研究胃肠功能和便秘的有用的非侵入性方法。

paras.en: Because bowel sounds can be monitored without more invasive procedures, researchers may be able to use the technique to track short term changes in intestinal movement and better understand how different behaviors or treatments affect the digestive system.
paras.zh: 由于无需进行更多侵入性操作即可监测肠鸣音，因此研究人员或许能够使用该技术来跟踪肠道运动的短期变化，并更好地了解不同的行为或治疗如何影响消化系统。

paras.en: Overall, the study provides a closer look at how rapidly the gut can respond to physical activity. Gut motility increased almost immediately after a 20 minute walk, offering a possible biological explanation for why movement can help relieve constipation.
paras.zh: 总的来说，这项研究让我们更仔细地了解肠道对身体活动的反应速度。步行 20 分钟后，肠道蠕动几乎立即增强，这为运动为何有助于缓解便秘提供了可能的生物学解释。

paras.en: The results also reinforce a broader message about digestive health: even relatively light physical activity may have effects on the gut much sooner than previously recognized.
paras.zh: 研究结果还强化了有关消化健康的更广泛信息：即使是相对较轻的体力活动也可能比之前认识的更快地对肠道产生影响。
